# Puzzle Jar: every question and answer

Source: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/ (updated 2026-11-24)

## Puzzle Jar: 20 puzzle games in one free app

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/

Puzzle Jar is a free iPhone and Android app with 20 shape-and-color puzzle games inside: you unscrew bolts, sort nuts and sweets, match buttons, untangle strings of lights, pop bubbles and more. Every game and every level plays offline, and you never need an account. We are Sultan of Niyyat, the small studio that made it; the app was called Route Duel before update 2.0.0 turned it into a collection.

### What is Puzzle Jar?

A collection of 20 small puzzle games that share one level count, one set of helpers and one jar. Each game has its own pieces and rules, from screws and nuts to beads, buses and bubbles, but they all work on shapes and colors rather than words or numbers. There is no clock in almost all of them, no lives and no waiting between levels. You can follow the level road through every game in turn or open any single game in Free play.

### Which 20 games are in Puzzle Jar?

These, in the order the level road visits them: Bolts & Jars : take screws out of stacked plates and fill jars by color. Sweet Stacks : move sweets between glass jars until each jar holds a single color. Button Tin : pick buttons off a pile and sew three of a kind together. Nut Sort : move painted nuts between bolts of different heights. Bead Swap : swap neighboring beads to make rows of three or more. Mosaic Tray : place tile pieces on an 8x8 tray and clear lines to free jewels. Toy Chest : slide blocks out through doors of their own color. Hop On : walk a crowd of passengers onto buses that match them. Pencil Case : tap pencils so they slide out, tip first, without bumping. Snug Skeins : unwind wool from felt toys into baskets. Shelf Sort : line up three matching goods on a shelf front. Treat Drop : drop sweets into a jar so two alike join into a bigger one. Honey Hive : stack hexagon honey tiles and collect ten of a color. Fruit Tumble : tap groups of touching fruit to pop them. Balloon Bunch : pop balloons that float upward and make fireworks. Tide Pool : clear sea creatures before new rows push up from below. Garland Tangle : move lanterns until no string of lights crosses another. Bubble Picnic : aim and shoot bubbles to pop groups of three. Quilt Pins : a logic grid with one pin in every patch, row and column. Route Duel : our original game, a turn-by-turn duel against a computer rival.

### How is Puzzle Jar different from a one-game puzzle app?

You get many genres in one download and one shared progress. A single screw or sort app gives you the same rule for hundreds of levels; here, three levels of one game are followed by three of another, so the puzzle changes before it gets old. Hints, take backs and rescues are shared by all 20 games, and so are the jar, the day streak and a Remove Ads purchase. One app also takes far less room on your phone than 20 separate ones.

### How does the level road work?

The road is one level number that runs through every game. You play three levels of a game, easy, then medium, then hard, and then the road moves to the next game; after the twentieth it starts again at the first, one step further on in each. Only levels won on the road move that number forward. Home shows your next road level and the six after it as small colored bubbles, so you always know which game is coming.

### What is the jar in Puzzle Jar?

A glass jar on Home that fills as you win. Every win, in any game, drops one piece into it in that game's color. Ten pieces fill it, and a full jar gives you one hint, one take back and one rescue, then empties so a fresh jar can start. Daily puzzles and Free play wins count too, so it fills however you like to play.

### What is Free play?

A row of cards on Home, one for each of the 20 games, all unlocked from the very first launch. Tap a card to play that game's next level, as many times as you want. Each game remembers its own level, so Free play moves that game forward, but it does not move the shared road number. Route Duel's card also holds Solo Run, the only timed mode in the app, which opens once you reach Route Duel's level 6.

### What are today's puzzles?

One extra puzzle per game, every day, shown under "Today's puzzles" on Home. They are separate from the normal levels: most games have 60 of them in each of three sets that take turns, so a daily does not come round again for about six months. Route Duel's daily is a picture board chosen by the date. Daily wins fill the jar and keep your streak going, but they do not change any game's own level.

### How does the day streak work?

It counts the days in a row on which you finished at least one level, in any of the 20 games. A day on which you won more than you lost is marked gold as a "winning day". If you miss a day after a streak of two days or more, you can save it by watching a short video that day or the next; after that it starts again from one.

### Which Puzzle Jar game should I start with?

Just tap Play: the road begins with Bolts & Jars, a screw puzzle with a guided first level that cannot be lost. If you already know what you like, go straight to that genre in Free play: Sweet Stacks or Nut Sort for sorting, Button Tin for tile matching, Bead Swap for match-3, Bubble Picnic for a bubble shooter. We put the two hardest games, Quilt Pins and Route Duel, at the end of the road on purpose.

### How long does a level take?

As long as you like in nearly every game, because there is no clock; you can put the phone down mid-level and come back. Early levels in each game are small and over quickly, while hard and boss levels ask for more planning. As one measured example, we built Honey Hive levels to last about two minutes. The single exception is Route Duel's Solo Run, a race against a clock of at least two minutes.

### Does Puzzle Jar have a story or characters?

No. There are no characters to follow, no dialogue and no house to decorate between levels. Each game is a plain puzzle made of shapes and colors: screws, sweets, buttons, beads, lanterns, sea creatures. The only opponent anywhere is Route Duel's computer rival, which plays routes against you on a board and has no story behind it.

### Do I need to read or do math to play Puzzle Jar?

No. While you play, everything is shown by color, shape and position, and each color also wears its own small symbol. Each game opens with a short rules card in simple English, and you can read it again from the "?" button, but you do not need it to tap and try. There are no number puzzles, no word games and no card games in the collection.

### Can I play only the games I like?

Yes. Free play lets you stay in one game, or a few, for as long as you want, and those wins still fill the jar and count toward your streak. The road number only moves when you play road levels, so it simply waits for you. Many players use the road for variety and Free play for a favorite.

### Is Puzzle Jar a new game?

It is a new name for an app that first came out on iPhone on October 19, 2026 as Route Duel, a single puzzle duel. Update 2.0.0 in November 2026 renamed it Puzzle Jar on the same App Store and Google Play pages and added more games; later updates grew it to 20. Players who already had Route Duel kept their levels and purchases, and Route Duel is still inside as the last game on the road.

## Bolts & Jars: the screw puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/bolts-and-jars-screw-puzzle/

Bolts & Jars is the screw puzzle in Puzzle Jar and the first game on its level road. Colored plates are stacked on top of each other and held down by screws. You tap screws to take them out, each screw flies into a jar of its own color, and you win when every jar is full. There is no clock and no move limit: you only lose if the waiting tray fills up and no screw can go anywhere.

### How do you play Bolts & Jars?

Tap a screw to unscrew it. If a jar of the same color is open, the screw flies straight in. If not, it waits in the tray at the bottom, which has 5 holes. Two jars are open at a time, and the game shows which jar comes next. Three screws fill a jar; a full jar leaves and the next one slides in.

### Why won't a screw come out when I tap it?

A plate lying on top of it is holding it in. In Bolts & Jars a screw can only leave when nothing above it covers its hole. Take out the screws of the plate on top first; once that plate has no screws left, it drops away and frees the screws under it.

### How do you win a level?

Fill every jar. When the last jar is full, the board is clear and the level is won. The number of jars is the real size of a level: early levels have only a few, and levels grow by about one jar per round of three.

### How do you lose in Bolts & Jars?

Only one way: the 5-hole tray is full and none of the screws you can reach matches an open jar. Then the game stops and offers a rescue, a fresh try or the way home. Running slowly never loses; you can stop and think for as long as you like.

### What is the best strategy for the screw puzzle?

Look before you tap. The jars tell you which colors are wanted now and next, so take screws of those colors first and leave the others where they are. A screw left on the board costs nothing; a screw sent to the tray takes one of only five holes. Treat the tray as emergency space, not a waiting room: on hard levels, a tray that fills early is the usual reason a run ends.

### Which plate should I clear first?

Usually the top plate that is hiding the most screws. Freeing one big plate can open three or four screws at once, which gives you choices. Clearing a small corner plate first often leaves you with nothing useful to tap.

### What do the symbols on the screws mean?

Each color has its own mark: a heart, a shield, a star, a tick, a bolt or an eye. The mark always goes with the same color, so you can play by shape alone. We added it so that players who find some colors hard to tell apart are never stuck guessing.

### What does a hint do in Bolts & Jars?

A hint makes one screw glow. It is a screw that is safe to take now, worked out by the same solver we use to check our levels, so it never walks you into a dead end. Hints are shared by all 20 games, so one spent here is one less for the others.

### Can I undo a move in the screw puzzle?

Yes. Take back puts your last screw back where it was. The first three take backs on every level are free; after that each one comes from your take-back count. With Remove Ads bought, take backs are unlimited.

### What is the "+1 hole" rescue?

When the tray is full and you are stuck, the rescue adds one more hole to the tray so you can keep going. You can use it up to twice on a level. The first rescue of a level can come from a short video you choose to watch; the next one uses a rescue from your count.

### Are Bolts & Jars levels possible without hints?

Yes. Every level is played through by a computer solver before it goes in the game, with no hints and no rescues, so a winning order of taps always exists. Hard and boss levels are meant to make you think; they are not set up to force a purchase.

### How hard does Bolts & Jars get?

It starts gentle: level 1 shows you where to tap and cannot be lost. Levels come in rounds of easy, medium and hard, and every fourth hard level is a boss. The game also follows how you play: two easy wins in a row make the next level a step harder, and a level you needed a retry or rescue for makes the next one a step easier.

### Is Bolts & Jars a good screw puzzle for adults?

We think so, and adults are who we made it for. There are no timers, no lives to wait for and no reading. It suits people who like to plan a few moves ahead and enjoy the click of a full jar, more than people who want speed or action.

## Sweet Stacks: the color sort puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/sweet-stacks-color-sort/

Sweet Stacks is the color sort game in Puzzle Jar and the second stop on the level road. Glass jars each hold up to four sweets in mixed colors; you move sweets from jar to jar until every jar holds four of one color and gets a lid. It plays like a ball sort or water sort puzzle, with no clock and no move limit, and here Undo is always free.

### How do you play Sweet Stacks?

Tap a jar to lift the sweet on top, then tap the jar you want it in. A sweet can only land on a sweet of its own color or in an empty jar. When four sweets of one color sit together in a jar, the jar gets a lid and is finished. Put a lid on every jar and the level is won.

### Why does Sweet Stacks move more than one sweet at a time?

Lifting a jar takes the top sweet together with every sweet of the same color directly under it, because a run of one color always travels as a group. They then fill the jar you tap only as far as it has room: a jar holds four, so if it already has three, only one sweet goes across and the rest stay where they were. Look at how much space a jar has before you choose it.

### Why won't a sweet go into the jar I tapped?

That jar is already full with four sweets, it already has its lid, or its top sweet is a different color. The game tells you which one it was in a short message. A sweet never goes on top of another color, even for a moment, so the only places it can go are a matching top sweet or a completely empty jar.

### What are the wrapped sweets in Sweet Stacks?

Sweets in a purple wrapper with a question mark, which hide their color until they become the top sweet of their jar. They appear from level 31 on hard and boss levels. Because you cannot see what is underneath, these levels reward clearing the jars that hold wrapped sweets early, so you find out the colors while you still have space to use what you learn.

### What is the best strategy for Sweet Stacks?

Keep an empty jar empty for as long as you can. An empty jar is the only place any color can go, so filling it with a single sweet just to make some move throws away your most flexible space. Prefer moves that put a sweet on its own color, and before each move, ask which jar it frees up. Work toward a lid: a finished jar takes four sweets off the board for good.

### Which jar should I work on first in Sweet Stacks?

Usually the one closest to being done or closest to being empty. A jar with three of a color on top needs only one more to get its lid; a jar with just one or two sweets in it can often be emptied in a move or two, which gives you a fresh empty jar. Jars that are full of mixed colors are the slow ones, so leave them until you have room to unpick them.

### Is undo free in Sweet Stacks?

Yes, always, and there is no limit. Sweet Stacks is the one game in Puzzle Jar where Undo never costs anything, on every level, with or without Remove Ads, and Again (start the level over) is free too. In the other games only the first three take backs of a level are free, unless you own Remove Ads. So in Sweet Stacks you can try an idea, see where it leads and step back as many times as you need.

### What happens when there are no moves left in Sweet Stacks?

A "No moves left!" card appears with your choices: add one empty jar, undo a few moves to try another order, or start again. The level waits for your choice; nothing runs out while you think. Sometimes you are not truly stuck but going round in circles between two empty jars; that is why the +1 Jar button sits in the bottom bar the whole time, not only on that card.

### What does the +1 Jar button do?

It adds one empty jar to the level, which is often all a hard sort needs. You can use it once per level. The first one can come from a short video you choose to watch; otherwise it uses one rescue from the count that all 20 games share. Once used on a level, the button shows a zero until the next level.

### What does a hint show in Sweet Stacks?

A hint lifts the right jar for you and puts a gold ring on the jar to drop the sweets in, so you only have to tap the ringed jar. The move comes from the same solver that checks our levels, which looks for the shortest sensible way to finish, so a hint is a move a good player would make. Each hint uses one from your shared hint count.

### How many colors are there in Sweet Stacks?

Up to 10. Level 1 has only three colors, then a new one comes in about every six rounds of the road. Each color also has its own small symbol, a heart, shield, star, tick, bolt, eye, triangle, plus, music note or gear, so two similar shades are never a guessing game. The symbol shows on the sweet and again on the lid of a finished jar.

### How hard does Sweet Stacks get?

Gentle at first: level 1 cannot be lost and levels 1 to 5 are only easy or medium. After that it follows the road's rounds of easy, medium and hard, with a boss on every fourth hard level. More colors and the wrapped sweets are what make later levels hard. Every level is played through by our solver with no extra jar before it ships, so the extra jar is a shortcut, never a requirement.

### Is Sweet Stacks like water sort and ball sort games?

Yes, it is the same family of color sort puzzle, played with sweets in jars instead of liquid in test tubes or balls in tubes. If you enjoy those, the rules will feel familiar within a level. What we changed is around the edges: free unlimited undo, a symbol on every color, wrapped sweets for later levels, and ads only between levels, never inside one.

## Button Tin: the triple tile match

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/button-tin-tile-match/

Button Tin is the triple tile match game in Puzzle Jar and the third game on the level road. Sewing buttons lie in a pile, up to five layers deep, inside a tin. You tap free buttons onto a card with seven spaces, three of a kind are sewn together and leave, and you win when the tin is empty. There is no clock and no move limit; the only danger is a full card.

### How do you play Button Tin?

Tap any button that has nothing lying on top of it. It jumps down to the button card under the tin and sits next to others of its kind. As soon as three alike are on the card, they are sewn together and disappear, which frees their spaces. A counter at the top shows how many buttons are still in the tin.

### Why can't I tap some buttons in Button Tin?

They are covered. A button is free only when no other button overlaps it from above, even by a small edge; covered buttons are drawn shaded so you can tell them apart. Take the buttons lying on top first and the one underneath lights up. On most levels you can still see a covered button's kind through the shade, which is useful for planning.

### How do you win Button Tin?

Empty the tin. Every kind of button comes in sets of three, so if you keep making threes, the last button taken always completes the last set. The counter at the top falls to zero and the tin is shown empty. Early levels have only a handful of buttons; later piles hold dozens.

### When are you stuck in Button Tin?

When all seven spaces on the card are filled and no three of them match. The game then shows a "Card full!" message with your ways out: add one more space to the card, take back a few buttons and try another order, start the level again, or go home. Nothing else ends a level, so slow, careful play is never punished.

### What is the best strategy for Button Tin?

Treat the card as seven spaces you can lose, not seven you can use. Every kind on the card that is not yet a pair is a space at risk, so the safest buttons to take are ones that make a three or turn a single into a pair. Taking a new kind when the card already holds four or five different ones is how most runs end. Count before you tap.

### Which buttons should I take first in Button Tin?

First, any free button that completes a three already on the card. Next, buttons that uncover the most others, often the ones near the top of a deep stack, because every button you reveal is another choice later. Since covered buttons are shaded but still show their kind on most levels, look for a pair hiding under one free button before you take it.

### What are face-down buttons in Button Tin?

Buttons that show only a question mark while something lies on them, so you cannot see their kind until they become free. They come in from level 31 on hard and boss levels. On those levels you lose the ability to plan from shaded buttons, so keep an extra space free on the card for surprises.

### What do the symbols on the buttons mean?

Each kind of button has a color and a matching symbol, such as a heart, a shield, a star, a tick, a lightning bolt or an eye. The pair never changes, so you can match by symbol alone if two colors look similar to you. On a busy pile, the symbol is often the quickest way to spot a third button.

### What does a hint do in Button Tin?

A hint makes one free button glow, and taking it keeps the level winnable. It is the first move of a winning order found by the solver we use to check every level, so it never leads you into a full card. Each hint uses one from the count shared by all 20 games, and you can use as many as you have.

### What does take back do in Button Tin?

It lifts the last button off the card and puts it back in its old place in the tin, where it covers the same buttons as before. The first three take backs of every level are free, and after that each one uses your shared take-back count. The full-card message offers it too, because stepping back two or three buttons is often enough.

### What is the +1 Space rescue?

It gives the card one more space, eight instead of seven, so a full card has room to finish a three. You can use it up to twice on one level. The first time on a level you can earn it with an optional video; the second uses a rescue from your shared count.

### How hard does Button Tin get?

Level 1 has nine buttons of three kinds and cannot be lost. Piles then grow slowly, to roughly 70 to 96 buttons, with more kinds and more layers, and boss levels add more buttons, an extra layer and one more kind on top of a normal hard level.

### Is Button Tin like a mahjong or triple tile match game?

It is a triple tile match: like mahjong solitaire, you can only take pieces that are free, but here you collect three of a kind on a card instead of pairing two. If you enjoy tile matching games where you clear a stack into a tray of seven, Button Tin plays the same way, with buttons, a shown count of what is left and no timer.

## Nut Sort: the nuts and bolts sort puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/nut-sort-nuts-and-bolts/

Nut Sort is the nuts and bolts sorting game in Puzzle Jar and the fourth game on the level road. Painted hex nuts sit mixed up on steel bolts; you move them between bolts until all four nuts of each color share one bolt and it gets a cap. What sets it apart is that the bolts are not all the same height. There is no clock and no move limit.

### How do you play Nut Sort?

Tap a bolt to lift its top nut, then tap another bolt to drop it. A nut can go onto a nut of the same color or onto an empty bolt, never onto a different color. Every color has exactly four nuts, and when all four stand alone on one bolt, a cap twists on and that bolt is done. Cap every color to win.

### Why are some bolts in Nut Sort taller or shorter?

To change how much room you have. An ordinary bolt holds four nuts, a tall bolt holds five, and a short helper bolt only two or three. You can tell them apart by the small notches at the foot of each bolt, one per space, with no numbers. From level 7 the mix changes from round to round: some boards are plain, some have a tall bolt, a short helper or both.

### Can a short bolt finish a color in Nut Sort?

No. A color needs all four of its nuts on one bolt, and a short helper bolt holds at most three, so it can never get a cap. Think of it as a parking spot: a safe place to put two or three nuts out of the way while you dig out what is underneath. It is still worth a lot, so try not to block it with a nut you have no plan for.

### Why did only some of my nuts move?

The bolt you dropped on ran out of room. A move lifts the top nut together with any nuts of the same color directly below it, and then puts as many as fit on the target bolt; the rest stay behind. Dark nuts never join that group, so a run of color stops at the first dark nut under it.

### What are dark nuts in Nut Sort?

Charcoal steel nuts with no color symbol, whose real color is hidden until they become the top nut on their bolt. Then the dark coat flakes off and you see what you have. They appear from level 16 on hard and boss levels, and from level 46 on some medium ones. On a dark level every nut under the top one of each bolt starts dark, so the whole board is a guess at first.

### What is the best strategy for Nut Sort?

Count the room before every move, not just the colors. Because bolts hold different numbers of nuts, the same move can leave one bolt with a free space or with none. Keep at least one bolt empty or nearly empty as long as you can, use the short helper to park nuts, and dig toward dark nuts early so you learn their colors while you still have space to act on them.

### Where should I finish a color in Nut Sort?

On an ordinary four-nut bolt when you have the choice. Once a bolt is capped, it is locked: nothing can be taken off it or added to it. If you cap a color on the tall bolt, its fifth space is locked away with it, and you lose the board's extra room. Use the tall bolt for juggling and let the plain bolts take the caps.

### What happens when there are no moves left in Nut Sort?

The game shows "No moves left!" and offers what still works: an extra empty bolt, a take back to step out of the dead end, starting the level again, or going home. Moving a single color's whole stack to an empty bolt of the same height changes nothing, so the game does not count it as a way out.

### What does +1 Bolt do in Nut Sort?

It adds one empty bolt with room for four nuts, enough to finish a whole color on it. You get one per level, and the button stays in the bottom bar the whole time. Pay for it either by watching an optional video or with one rescue from the count shared by all 20 games.

### How do hints and take backs work in Nut Sort?

A hint lifts the right bolt and puts a gold ring around the bolt to drop on, a safe move found by our solver; it uses one shared hint. Take back undoes your last move, and the first three on every level are free, then each uses one from your count. Unlike Sweet Stacks, where undo costs nothing, take backs here are limited unless you own Remove Ads.

### How is Nut Sort different from Bolts & Jars?

They share a hardware look but are different puzzles. In Bolts & Jars you take screws out of stacked plates and send them away into jars, so the board empties and the question is which screw to take next. In Nut Sort nothing leaves the board: every nut stays on a bolt and you rearrange them, so the question is where to put each one.

### How is Nut Sort different from Sweet Stacks?

Both are color sorts, but Sweet Stacks uses jars that all hold four, while Nut Sort mixes four-, five- and two- or three-space bolts, so room becomes part of the puzzle. Hidden pieces also arrive sooner here, from level 16 rather than 31, and the board's shape keeps changing. Sweet Stacks has free unlimited undo; Nut Sort gives three free take backs a level.

### How hard does Nut Sort get?

Level 1 has three colors and cannot be lost, and levels 1 to 5 are easy or medium. Colors build up to a maximum of 10, each with its own symbol on the nut and the cap.

## Bead Swap: the match-3 game

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/bead-swap-match-3/

Bead Swap is the match-3 game in Puzzle Jar: glass beads in a wooden craft tray. Swipe a bead onto its neighbor to line up three or more of one color; they clear and the beads above drop down. Each level sets goals at the top, such as collecting beads, melting wax, breaking crates or bringing brass buttons down, and gives you between 15 and 38 moves to reach them.

### How do you play Bead Swap?

Swipe one bead onto the bead next to it, up, down, left or right. If the swap makes a line of three or more of one color, the line clears, the beads above fall into the space and new beads drop in from the top. Watch the goal counters above the tray; when every one reaches zero, the level is won.

### Why did my swap slide back in Bead Swap?

Because it did not line anything up. A swap that makes no match of three slides straight back to where it was, and it costs no move. So a mistaken swipe is harmless; only swaps that clear something take a move off your count.

### What do the needle, burst and rainbow beads do?

Needle (line up 4 in a row): clears its whole row or column. Burst (an L or T shape): clears the squares around it. Rainbow bead (5 in a row): clears every bead of the color you swap it with. Tap a needle or burst, or swap it, to set it off; a rainbow bead goes off when you swap it with a bead of the color you want gone. The first time a level makes each kind of special, a short tip under the tray says what it does.

### What happens if I swap two special beads together?

You get a bigger blast than either would make alone. A needle with a needle clears a row and a column; a burst with a needle sweeps three rows and three columns; two bursts clear a big square; a rainbow bead with another special turns every bead of that color into the same special; and two rainbow beads clear the whole tray. Saving specials until two sit side by side is often worth a move.

### How do you clear wax and crates in Bead Swap?

Wax melts when beads lying on it clear, so make matches right on top of the wax spots. Crates break when beads next to them clear, so match alongside them. Thick wax (from level 19) and strong crates (from level 25) need two hits each. Needles and bursts help a lot, since one blast can hit several spots at once.

### How do you get the brass buttons down?

Clear the beads underneath them. Buttons fall like beads but can never be matched, and they count only when they reach the bottom row. A needle running up a button's column is the quickest way to drop it several squares at once. Buttons arrive on Bead Swap level 13.

### What are the holes in the Bead Swap tray?

They are gaps, squares where no bead can sit. From level 10 some trays have cut corners, a hole in the middle or notches in the sides. Beads still fall straight down, slipping past the gap, so the columns keep filling, but a gap breaks up lines and limits where you can match.

### What happens when you run out of moves in Bead Swap?

The level stops and offers +5 MOVES, a fresh try or the way home. +5 MOVES can be used up to twice on a level; the first time you can earn it with a short video you choose, the second time it uses a rescue. A take back also hands back the move it undoes.

### Are Bead Swap levels rigged so you need to pay?

No. The beads that drop in are fixed for each level, so a level plays out the same way every time and can never turn harder in secret. Before a level ships, a computer player wins it with no help, and our tests replay that win. If the tray ever has no possible swap, the beads are mixed, and that is fixed too.

### Why is a bead glowing when I didn't ask for a hint?

That is the free nudge. If you do nothing for 6 seconds, Bead Swap makes a working swap glow, as most match-3 games do. It is free and only shows a swap that matches; it is not the best move. The paid HINT is the one that looks for the best swap.

### How does the Bead Swap hint choose a move?

It plays out every possible swap, knowing which beads will drop in next, and shows the one that does most for your goals. That is more than a person can see from the board, which is why it can point at a move that looks plain but sets up a chain. Hints are shared by all 20 games.

### What is the best strategy for Bead Swap?

Spend moves on goals, not on pretty matches. Check which counters are furthest from zero and work there first. Make a needle or burst whenever you can, and aim it: a needle placed in a column full of wax does several moves' work. Late in a level, count your moves left against what remains, and use specials before you run out rather than saving them.

### How hard does Bead Swap get?

Trays grow from 7 by 7 to 9 by 9 squares, and new obstacles come one at a time: wax at level 3, crates at 7, gaps at 10, buttons at 13, then thick wax and strong crates. Five colors are in play, six on later boss levels. Hard levels give just enough moves for a good plan, with little to spare.

## Mosaic Tray: the block puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/mosaic-tray-block-puzzle/

Mosaic Tray is the block puzzle in Puzzle Jar. You drag pieces of glazed tiles onto an 8 by 8 wooden tray, and any row or column filled from end to end clears. Some tiles hold jewels; clear the lines they sit in to collect them, and collect every jewel to win. Unlike endless block games, each level has a set number of pieces, dealt in a fixed order, so every level plays the same way each time and can be won.

### How do you play Mosaic Tray?

Drag a piece from the three under the tray and drop it where it fits. While you drag, the spot it would land on shows faintly and any lines it would complete glow. Fill a row or column and it clears. When you have placed all three pieces, the next three are dealt. The jewel counter at the top shows how many are left to free.

### How do you collect the jewels in Mosaic Tray?

Complete the row or the column a jewel tile sits in. When that line clears, the jewel flies up to the counter. Each jewel starts in its own row and column, so you choose which way to free it: across or down. Pick whichever line is closer to full.

### Can you rotate pieces in Mosaic Tray?

No. Pieces go on the tray the way they are dealt. That is part of the planning: a long upright piece only fits a column gap, so keep space for the shapes you can see coming rather than counting on turning them.

### Why does Mosaic Tray have a piece limit?

Because it turns the tray into a puzzle with an answer. The pile next to the jewel counter shows how many pieces the level gives, from 9 to 45. Endless block games deal at random, and a common complaint about them is a hand that cannot fit however well you play. Here the order is fixed and our level maker has already won with exactly that pile.

### How do you lose a level of Mosaic Tray?

Either none of the pieces in your hand fits anywhere on the tray, or the pile runs out while jewels are still waiting. The hand shakes red and a card offers a rescue, a take back, a new try or the way home. There is no clock.

### What is a good Mosaic Tray strategy?

Work toward the jewels, not toward tidy lines. Clearing a row with no jewel in it feels good but spends pieces. Keep the middle of the tray open, because the bigger pieces need room, and fill toward edges and corners first. Before you drop a piece, check whether it blocks the only spot where the next large shape could go.

### Does clearing several lines at once help in Mosaic Tray?

Yes, in two ways. A double or triple clear frees more of the tray for the pieces still to come, and it can collect two jewels with one piece. Clears made with pieces in a row also show "Combo x2" and up. The combo words are for fun; what matters is the space and the jewels.

### What does the hint do in Mosaic Tray?

It shows a safe place for one of your pieces: a spot from which the level can still be won with the pieces left. Before showing it, the solver plays the rest of the level through. If no win is left from where you are, no hint is charged, which is your sign to take back or try again.

### What does Take back undo in Mosaic Tray?

It lifts the last piece off the tray, and if that piece cleared lines, the tiles and jewels in those lines come back too. That makes it safe to test an idea: drop a piece, see what it leaves, and lift it off again. Each level gives three take backs for free.

### What does the Mosaic Tray rescue give you?

Room to move. Your stuck hand is swapped for single tiles, three more singles follow, and ten extra pieces are added to the pile. Single tiles fit any empty square, so they can finish an almost-full row. You can rescue up to twice on one level.

### Is Mosaic Tray like other block puzzles?

It uses the same 8 by 8 board and row-and-column clears as the popular endless block puzzles, but every level is a set puzzle with jewels to collect and a fixed pile of pieces. You will not get a run ruined by a random bad hand. If you prefer endless high-score play, that is the one thing Mosaic Tray does not offer.

### How hard does Mosaic Tray get?

Level 1 has two jewels and a glowing guide on each turn, and cannot be lost. From there, levels come in rounds of easy, medium and hard. Hard and boss levels put more jewels on the tray, deal fewer small pieces and more awkward ones, and leave little or no spare in the pile, so expect to think a few pieces ahead.

## Toy Chest: the color block jam

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/toy-chest-block-jam/

Toy Chest is the color block jam in Puzzle Jar. Painted wooden blocks sit on a grid inside a toy chest, and the chest's walls have colored doors. Drag a block and it slides through empty squares; when it reaches a door of its own color that is wide enough, it slides out. Get every block out to win. There is no clock, only a number of moves, and each drag uses one.

### How do you play Toy Chest?

Put your finger on a block and drag it toward a door of the same color. It moves through empty squares only, never through another block or a stone. Once it touches its door, it shoots out of the chest. The counter at the top shows how many blocks are left and how many moves you have.

### Why won't my block go out through the door?

Usually one of two reasons. The door is not its color, or the door is too slim for the block. Doors are one to three squares wide, and a block only leaves through a door at least as wide as the side it is pushing through. A three-wide block needs a three-wide door of its color, or a different way round.

### Does every drag in Toy Chest cost a move?

Yes, one drag is one move, however far the block slides. That is the whole dial of the game: hard levels give just enough moves for a good plan. A long slide across the chest costs the same as a one-square nudge, so make each drag count.

### How do you lose in Toy Chest?

You run out of moves with blocks still in the chest, or no block can move at all. Then the blocks wiggle red and the game offers a rescue, a fresh try or home. Since there is no clock, you can take as long as you like over each drag.

### What are the gray stones in Toy Chest?

Fixed obstacles. Stones arrive at Toy Chest level 7, never move and never leave; blocks have to go round them. They often turn a short exit into a longer path, so look for them before you plan a block's route.

### How do two-color blocks work?

A two-color block has an outer color and an inner one. Slide it to a door of the outer color and that layer peels off; the same block, now in its inner color, then needs a door of that color. Two-color blocks appear from level 16. Each one takes at least two moves, so count them twice when you plan.

### What do ice, one-way blocks and locks do?

Ice (from level 31): a frozen block cannot move until a set number of other blocks have left the chest. One-way blocks (from level 46): they slide only across, or only up and down. Locks (from level 61): locked blocks open once the block carrying the key has left. Each new obstacle gets a short card the first time it shows up.

### What is the best strategy for Toy Chest?

Find the blocks that are in everyone's way and plan their exits first. A block that can leave right now is rarely the wrong move, but check where it goes, because a block parked in front of another door costs you a move later. On levels with locks or ice, the key block and the blocks that thaw the ice come first.

### What does the Toy Chest hint show?

The next move of a win the solver found within the moves you have left. The game keeps that plan, so as long as you follow the hints, they never lead you astray. If you take your own route halfway, the next hint plans again from where you are.

### What does the Toy Chest rescue do?

Two things at once: it gives you five more moves, or enough to bring every block left out with two to spare, whichever is more, and it lets you lift any one block straight out of the chest. You choose the block, so pick the one jamming everything. A level allows two rescues.

### How hard does Toy Chest get?

Level 1 has three blocks, a glowing guide and cannot be lost. Grids grow from 5 by 5 to 8 by 8 and blocks from one to six squares. New obstacles join one at a time, from stones at level 7 to locks at level 61. Every fourth hard level is a boss, like the one in the picture, and an easy level always follows a hard one.

### Why does Toy Chest count moves instead of time?

Because a clock punishes slow thinkers, and puzzles should reward thinking. Countdown clocks are a common complaint about color block jam games, so we left the clock out and limited moves instead. You can stop mid-level and think for as long as you like; the only pressure is the move count.

## Hop On: the bus jam puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/hop-on-bus-jam-puzzle/

Hop On is the bus jam puzzle in Puzzle Jar. Painted passengers crowd a town square, and buses pull up one at a time along the top. Tap a passenger who has a clear way out: they walk to the stop and board if the bus is their color, or sit on the waiting bench if not. Get everyone on a bus to win. There is no clock and no move limit; you only get stuck when the bench is full and nobody can board.

### How do you play Hop On?

Tap a passenger. If an open path leads from them to the stop, they hop out of the crowd. A passenger whose color matches the bus at the stop takes a seat; anyone else waits on the bench. A bus with all seats filled drives off, the next one pulls in, and any bench passengers of its color hop straight on.

### Why won't a passenger move when I tap them?

They are boxed in. A passenger can only leave if there is a free way through the crowd to the stop; other passengers and planters block it. The passenger shakes and the game tells you why. Clear the people between them and the stop first.

### What happens when the Hop On bench is full?

You can still tap anyone whose color matches the bus at the stop. But once the bench is full and no one who can walk out matches the bus, the level is stuck: the crowd shakes and the bench flashes red. The bench has 4 to 7 seats, shown at the top as free seats.

### What are hidden passengers in Hop On?

Passengers whose color you cannot see yet. They appear from Hop On level 8. A hidden passenger shows their color as soon as they have a free way to the stop, and it stays shown after that. Until then, plan around them: you know they are one of the colors still in the bus line.

### What are the brick doorways for?

A doorway holds a line of passengers who step out one by one. The number on the doorway shows how many are still inside. Each time the square in front of it empties, the next one steps out. Doorways start at level 20 and are easy to forget, so count their passengers when you plan the bench.

### What are frozen passengers?

Passengers who cannot move until a certain number of other passengers have left the square. They arrive at level 35. They thaw by themselves as the crowd thins, so you never need to free them directly, but they can block a path for a while.

### What changes with two bus stops and big buses?

From level 50 some squares have two stops, so two buses wait at once and you have two colors to fill. From level 65 big buses arrive with six seats instead of three. Both give you more choice, and more ways to clog the bench if you send people out in the wrong order.

### What is the best strategy for Hop On?

Read the bus line before you tap. The next buses are always shown, so look for passengers of those colors who can already walk out, and leave the others in the crowd. A passenger standing in the square costs nothing; one on the bench takes a seat you may need later. Use the bench to unblock a path, not as a waiting room.

### How do you win a level of Hop On?

Get every passenger onto a bus. Each color has exactly enough passengers to fill its buses, so no seat is ever left over or short. The counter in the top corner shows how many passengers are still to go.

### What does the Hop On hint show?

The next tap in a winning order the solver found with the bench as it is now. The game keeps that whole order, so if you follow the hints from there, each one leads to the next and none of them traps you.

### What does the rescue do in Hop On?

It adds two seats to the bench and lets one passenger of your choice hop straight out, even someone stuck in the middle of the crowd. Choose the passenger who is blocking the most others, or one whose bus is next. You can use it up to twice on one level.

### How hard does Hop On get?

Level 1 has 12 passengers in two colors, five bench seats and a glowing guide, and cannot be lost. The square grows from 3 by 4 up to 7 by 8, and new things join one at a time: planters at level 5, hidden passengers at 8, doorways at 20 and so on. Hard levels mix up the order of the buses.

### Is Hop On a bus jam game without a timer?

Yes. Hop On is the crowd kind of bus jam: you walk people to the bus rather than sliding buses out of a car park. There is no countdown and no passenger who explodes on a timer. You can think about each tap as long as you need.

## Pencil Case: the tap-away puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/pencil-case-tap-away-puzzle/

Pencil Case is the tap-away puzzle in Puzzle Jar. Colored pencils lie in an open case, each pointing up, down, left or right, and a tapped pencil slides out the way its sharpened tip points. If another pencil is in the way, it bumps and you lose one of three hearts. Take every pencil out to win; lose all three hearts and the level is over, with a rescue, a take back or a fresh try on offer.

### How do you play Pencil Case?

Look at the tip, then tap. The sharpened end shows which way a pencil will travel. If the whole lane from the tip to the edge of the case is empty, the pencil shoots out. If anything sits in that lane, even far down it, the pencil slides up to it, knocks it and slides back. The case starts at 4 by 4 squares and grows to 9 by 12 over the levels.

### Why did I lose a heart in Pencil Case?

You tapped a pencil whose path was blocked. Each new bump costs one heart, and the level gives you three, shown as heart shapes at the top. The blocker is often a long pencil lying across the lane a few squares away, which is easy to miss on a big case. Tapping a clipped pencil before its turn also counts as a bump.

### Does tapping the same blocked pencil twice cost two hearts?

No. If a pencil has already bumped and no other pencil has left the case since, tapping it again only makes it wiggle. We added this because a nervous double tap should not cost you the level. Once any pencil leaves, the slate is wiped, and a fresh bump costs a heart again.

### What does the clip on a pencil mean?

A clipped pencil must leave last of its color. Clips start appearing on Pencil Case level 16. The steel clip stays on until every other pencil of that color is gone; then it pops off and the pencil can slide out like any other. So when you see a clip, count the other pencils of its color and plan to free them first.

### What are the erasers for?

They are fixed walls. Erasers arrive from level 10, never move and never need clearing. No pencil ever points at an eraser, so one is never in a pencil's way. What they do is take up squares, which shapes where pencils can lie and makes the case harder to read at a glance.

### How do you lose a level of Pencil Case?

By running out of hearts. There is no move count and no clock, so slow thinking is free; only bumps hurt. When the third heart breaks, an "Out of hearts" card offers +HEARTS, TAKE BACK, TRY AGAIN and HOME.

### What is the safest way to clear a crowded pencil case?

Trace each lane all the way to the edge before you tap. Start with pencils that point outward along an edge, since nothing can sit in front of them. Then ask which pencil, once gone, opens the most lanes for others; long pencils lying across the middle are usually the ones holding everything up. Taking a pencil out never blocks anything new, so a free pencil is always a safe tap.

### Is there always a way to clear the case without losing a heart?

Yes. When we make a level, any pencils that would block each other forever are turned round or removed, and a computer then takes every pencil out without a single bump. Our tests replay that clean run on every level before it ships. Hearts are there to forgive slips, not to make up for a broken board.

### What does the hint do in Pencil Case?

It makes one pencil glow that can leave right now. Of the free pencils, it picks the one that opens the way for the most others, so following hints also teaches you how to read the case. Since removing a pencil can never close a lane, a hinted pencil is never a trap.

### Does Take back give my heart back?

Yes. In Pencil Case, taking back a bump returns the heart it cost, and taking back a pencil that left puts it back in its place. The first three take backs on each level cost nothing; after that they come from the take-back count all 20 games share.

### What does +HEARTS do?

It fills your three hearts again and adds two golden hearts on top, five in all. It works once per level. The +HEARTS button sits in the bottom bar and can be used as soon as a heart is missing, or from the "Out of hearts" card. Watching a video you pick pays for it; so does one rescue from your count.

### How hard does Pencil Case get?

Level 1 cannot be lost, because every pencil on it can leave from the start. After that the case grows slowly, changes shape from round to round (wide, square, tall), and the pencils get longer, up to four squares. Erasers join at level 10 and clips at 16. Rounds go easy, medium, hard, with a boss every fourth hard level, and an easy level always comes after a hard one.

### Who is Pencil Case for?

Players who like quick, clean puzzles with a small sting for carelessness. There is no luck involved: the only skill is noticing what is in the way. If you enjoy the popular tap-to-clear direction puzzles, this is our take on that genre, with pencils, clips and erasers instead of plain shapes.

## Snug Skeins: the yarn unwind puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/snug-skeins-yarn-sort/

Snug Skeins is the yarn sort game in Puzzle Jar. Little felt animals peek out of balls of wool, each wound in several layers. Tap a toy and its outer layer unwinds into the wicker basket of that color; if no such basket is out yet, the skein waits in the sewing tin. Fill and send away every basket to win. There is no clock and no move count.

### How do you play Snug Skeins?

Tap any toy. Its outer layer of wool flies off as a skein. Two baskets sit on the shelf at a time and each holds three skeins; if one of them matches the skein's color, it lands there. Otherwise it drops into a spot in the sewing tin. A full basket lifts away, the next one comes out, and it collects any skeins of its color from the tin.

### What do the numbers and small balls on the toys mean?

The number is how many layers of wool that toy has left. The small ball next to it is the color of the next layer, the one you will uncover after this tap. Reading that second color is the key to the game: a tap that looks safe now might expose a color you have no basket for.

### Why did my tap get refused in Snug Skeins?

Because the skein had nowhere to go: no open basket of its color and no free spot in the sewing tin. The game refuses that tap with a short word rather than ending the level. Look for a toy whose outer color matches a basket that is already out.

### How do you lose in Snug Skeins?

Only when no tap is left: every toy's next skein would need a tin spot and the tin is full. Then the toys shake, the tin flashes red, and you can rescue, take back, try again or go home. Because a bad tap is refused first, you rarely lose by accident; you lose by filling the tin with colors that are a long way off.

### What is the sewing tin for?

It is your spare space: 4 to 7 spots, shown in a row under the baskets. Skeins wait there until a basket of their color comes out. The tin is the whole puzzle in Snug Skeins. Every skein you park there is a spot you cannot use again until its basket arrives.

### What are tied toys and pinned toys?

Both are toys you cannot tap yet. A tied toy, from level 8, wears a red bow with a strand of wool running to another toy; it opens once that other toy is bare. A pinned toy, from level 40, has a gold safety pin that comes out once the basket marked with a gold pin is filled and gone.

### What are hidden wool and thick wool?

Hidden wool, from level 15, shows a "?" instead of the next layer's color, so you only find out what is under it by tapping. Thick wool, from level 25, is a single layer that counts as two skeins at once: it can fill most of a basket in one tap, or take two tin spots.

### What is the best strategy for Snug Skeins?

Tap toys whose outer color goes straight into a basket, and among those, prefer the ones whose next color is also a basket that is out or coming soon. The next three baskets are shown on the shelf. Leave toys with far-off colors alone. If you must use the tin, park colors whose basket is next in line, not the ones at the back of the queue.

### What does the Snug Skeins hint do?

It points to the next tap of a winning order that the solver worked out from where you stand. That order is remembered, so a player who keeps following hints will finish the level without the tin ever overflowing.

### What does the Snug Skeins rescue give you?

Three helps at once. The tin gets two extra spots, one more basket comes out on the shelf, and the next basket of the color with the most skeins waiting in the tin comes out right away and takes them. That usually clears most of the tin in a single step. You can use it up to twice a level.

### How hard does Snug Skeins get?

Level 1 has three toys in two colors with a glowing guide, and cannot be lost. Levels grow to as many as 12 toys with up to 7 layers each. Hard and boss levels shuffle the basket order much more, so the color you need is often several baskets away. Big baskets that hold six skeins arrive at level 60.

### Is Snug Skeins a wool sort or a yarn knitting game?

It is the unwind kind of yarn game. You do not knit a picture or feed spools onto a belt; you unwind layers off toys and sort the wool into baskets by color. If you like color sorting with a little planning ahead, and a cozy look, it is a good fit.

## Shelf Sort: the goods sorting game

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/shelf-sort-goods-sorting/

Shelf Sort is the goods sorting game in Puzzle Jar. A wooden cupboard holds small shelves of painted goods, three spots to a shelf. Move goods one at a time onto shelves with a free spot; three of the same kind side by side in front pop. Empty a shelf's front and the row behind steps forward. Clear every shelf to win. There is no timer and no move count; you lose only if every spot fills up.

### How do you play Shelf Sort?

Drag an item onto another shelf that has a free spot, or tap the item and then tap the shelf. When the front of a shelf holds three of the same kind, they pop and leave. Goods come in twelve kinds, each with its own outline, from teacups and teddies to cacti and gift boxes, so you can sort by shape even if colors are hard for you to tell apart.

### What are the dimmed goods behind the shelves?

The next row. Each shelf can hide more goods behind the front one, shown faded so you can plan for them. Little boxes on the plank tell you how many rows still wait there. When you empty a shelf's front, that row slides forward and fills it again.

### Should I empty a shelf to reveal the row behind?

Only when you are ready for what is behind it. Emptying a front shows new goods, which can give you the third item you need. But those goods take up the spots you just freed. Check the dimmed row first: if it brings kinds you can already match, go ahead; if it brings three strangers, clear somewhere else.

### How do you lose in Shelf Sort?

Mainly by filling every spot in the cupboard, so no item has anywhere to go. The card says "No room left", with take back, an extra shelf, a fresh try or home. The game also stops you with a "No way to clear" card if it works out that no win is left from where you are. There is no clock and no count of moves.

### What does "Going round in circles?" mean in Shelf Sort?

It is a friendly check, not a loss. If you make 40 moves in a row without a single pop, the game offers help: take back, +1 shelf, try again, or KEEP TRYING to carry on as you were. We put it in place of the timer many sorting games use, so you are never cut off, just asked.

### How do locked shelves open in Shelf Sort?

By playing. A locked shelf, from level 10, holds goods under a padlock with one to three rings. Each time goods pop anywhere in the cupboard, a ring lights up; when all its rings are lit, the lock bursts open. No locked shelf in this game needs an ad or a payment to open.

### What are the shelves with a sign?

Picky shelves. From level 31 some empty shelves carry a sign showing one kind of goods, and they only take that kind. They are useful for finishing a set but can also leave you short of space. From the same level some kinds come six times, so you may pop the same goods twice.

### What is a good Shelf Sort strategy?

Gather pairs. Move items next to their match before you hunt for the third, and keep at least one shelf with free spots as working space. Look at the dimmed rows when you choose which shelf to empty. When locks are on the board, any pop helps open them, so quick, easy pops come first.

### What does the Shelf Sort hint show?

It lifts one item and rings the shelf to put it on. The move comes from our solver and is safe: following it keeps a win possible. If the solver finds no safe move from where you are, the game says so and keeps your hint, which is your cue to take back a few moves.

### What does +1 SHELF do?

It adds one empty shelf to the cupboard, three new spots to sort into. It is Shelf Sort's rescue and works once per level; the button sits in the bottom bar the whole time and also appears on the "No room left" card. You pay for it with a video you choose to watch or with one rescue from your shared count.

### How hard does Shelf Sort get?

Level 1 cannot be lost by anyone, and the next good move is always lifted and ringed for you. From there, cupboards range from 3 to 7 shelves. The difficulty is mostly in how mixed the goods are: easy levels keep each shelf close to one kind, while boss levels scatter nearly two kinds per shelf, with rows behind, locks and picky shelves.

### Why does Shelf Sort have no timer?

Because players of goods sorting games often complain about strict level timers, and about locked boxes that need an ad to open. So Shelf Sort has neither a timer nor a move count, and its locked shelves open only through play. Every level is checked by computer to be winnable without any help.

## Treat Drop: the drop and merge game

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/treat-drop-merge-game/

Treat Drop is the drop and merge game in Puzzle Jar, the kind where fruit or sweets fall into a jar and join. Slide to aim the sweet held over the glass jar and let go to drop it. When two of the same sweet touch, they join into the next size up. Each level asks you to make certain sweets, such as two tarts, from a set number of drops, while keeping the jar below the dotted line.

### How do you play Treat Drop?

Touch the screen and slide left or right; the sweet above the jar follows your finger. Let go and it drops, rolls and settles against the others with a small bounce. Two of the same kind that touch join into the next kind. The goals at the top count what you have made, and the pill on the right shows how many sweets you have left to drop.

### What are all the sweets in Treat Drop, from smallest to biggest?

There are ten, each made by joining two of the one before: sprinkle, gumball, mint, macaron, cookie, donut, tart, pie, cake and rainbow lolly. Two rainbow lollies that touch burst and leave the jar. Only the two to five smallest kinds are ever dropped; everything bigger you have to build.

### What happens if sweets go over the dotted line?

If a sweet comes to rest above the dotted line near the top of the jar, or stays above it for about 2 seconds, the jar has overflowed and you are stuck. A sweet that is still falling through the line does not count. While anything is above it, the line pulses red as a warning.

### How do you win a level of Treat Drop?

Make every sweet the goals ask for before your drops run out. Goals go up to pies: making cakes would take far too many drops for one level. On some levels the goal is two kinds at once, as in the picture, where one pie and five donuts are wanted.

### How do you lose in Treat Drop?

Two ways: you run out of sweets before the goals are met, or the jar overflows past the dotted line. In practice, running out of sweets is the more common one. Either way the game offers a rescue, a take back, a new try or the way home.

### Can you see which sweet is coming next?

Yes, one ahead. The next sweet waits in the small NEXT box on the right side of the jar. The order of drops is fixed for each level, so a level always gives the same sweets in the same order, and a second try lets you plan with what you learned.

### Does it matter where I drop each sweet?

Yes, a lot. Sweets grip each other and tend to stay close to where they land, so dropping everything in one spot rarely builds what you need. We widened the jars and tuned the friction so that dropping in one spot wins far fewer hard levels than aiming does. Aim each sweet at its twin, or at a gap where its twin will land next.

### What is the best strategy for Treat Drop?

Keep the big sweets together on one side and the small ones on the other. A pile sorted by size lets each new join land next to the one it should join next, which can set off a chain. Look at the NEXT sweet before you drop the current one, and leave room for it. Try not to bury a small sweet under big ones, where its twin cannot reach it.

### Why are there sweets already in the jar at the start?

From Treat Drop level 10, some levels begin with a few sweets placed in the jar. They can be a head start, if they match what you need, or an obstacle you have to build around. Either way, the level was won by our computer player with exactly that start.

### What does the Treat Drop hint do?

It shows the best spot for the sweet you are holding. Before answering, it tries every spot with the jar's real physics and plays the next four sweets ahead. In our tests it played about as well as the best tenth of our computer test players, where a hint that only looked at the matching sweet was merely average.

### What does the Treat Drop rescue give you?

More sweets to drop, from 3 to 18 depending on the level. If you got stuck because the jar overflowed, the rescue also lifts the little sweets out of the jar so there is room again. A level allows up to two rescues.

### How is Treat Drop different from endless merge games?

It has levels with goals and a fixed number of sweets, instead of one endless jar played for a high score. It also starts gently: level 1 asks for one cookie and shows the best spot for every sweet, and cannot be lost. Ads appear only between levels, never after drops.

## Honey Hive: the hexa sort puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/honey-hive-hexa-sort/

Honey Hive is the hexa sort game in Puzzle Jar. You drag stacks of six-sided honey tiles onto a honeycomb; when a stack lands next to one with the same color on top, those tiles hop over and pile up together. Ten or more of one color on top are collected, and you win by collecting the number of tiles the honey bar asks for. There is no clock and no move limit: the only way to lose is a comb with no free cell left.

### How do you play Honey Hive?

Drag one of the three stacks in the tray onto any empty cell of the comb. Each stack holds 2 to 6 tiles in one to three colors, and only the color on top matters for merging. If a stack in a touching cell shows the same color on top, those tiles hop across one by one. Once all three tray stacks are placed, three new ones are dealt.

### Why did my tiles keep hopping after I dropped a stack?

One drop can start a chain. After tiles hop onto the stack you placed, the stack they left shows a new color on top, and if that color matches one of its own neighbors, it pulls tiles in turn. Collected tiles do the same thing. Looking at what lies just under each top layer is how you predict a chain, and with practice, how you set one up on purpose.

### What does the number on a Honey Hive stack mean?

It counts the tiles of one color sitting on top of that stack, down to the first tile of a different color. A stack showing 8 needs only 2 more of its color to reach 10 and be collected. Tiles lower down in other colors don't count until everything above them is gone.

### How do you win a level of Honey Hive?

Collect the number of tiles the honey bar asks for, for example "0 of 80 tiles collected" at the start of a level. Tiles are collected when 10 or more of one color sit on top of a stack: they burst and fly to the bar, and whatever was underneath stays on the cell, or the cell empties. Goals run from 20 tiles on level 1 to as many as about 160 on the biggest boss levels, and most levels take about two minutes.

### How do you lose in Honey Hive?

The comb fills up. When every open cell already holds a stack and a stack from the tray has nowhere to go, the stacks shake and you are stuck. You can then rescue, take back a drop, try the level again or go home. Taking your time never counts against you, because nothing counts your drops.

### Where should I place a stack in Honey Hive?

Beside the stacks whose top color it matches, and away from colors it would block. A stack with red on top dropped between two blue stacks stops both of them from merging until the red is gone. Push messy, many-colored stacks toward the edges and keep the middle of the comb for merges, since a middle cell touches six others and an edge cell touches fewer.

### How many empty cells should I keep free?

As many as you can, and never count on the last one. All three stacks in the tray need a home before new ones arrive, so a comb with one or two free cells can be lost even when it looks fine.

### What are the dark locked cells in Honey Hive?

Cells you can't use yet. Each one shows a number, the tiles you still need to collect before it opens, and it counts down as you play. They first appear at level 12. A cell that opens gives you room exactly when the comb is getting crowded, so collecting early also buys space. No cell in Honey Hive is ever opened by watching an ad.

### What are iced stacks?

Stacks frozen in place on the comb, from level 25. An iced stack takes no part in merges until 10 tiles are collected on a cell right next to it, which cracks the ice. They build on an idea from level 5, where some levels start with stacks already on the comb, so you plan around them from your very first drop. Each new piece gets a short card the first time it shows up.

### Which stack and cell does the Honey Hive hint pick?

It shows which tray stack to drop and on which cell. To pick it, the game tries every empty cell for every stack in the tray and plays the six best choices through the rest of the tray before it decides. Because each level deals the same stacks in the same order every time, a hint means the same thing on a retry as on the first try.

### What does the bee rescue do?

Bees fly in and carry off the most mixed-up stacks on the comb, between 2 and 6 depending on the level, which clears room to keep going. Each level allows two. The first is offered for an optional video; if you skip that or want a second, it is paid from your stock of rescues.

### Can I undo a drop in Honey Hive?

Yes. Take back puts the last stack back in the tray and reverses the hops and collections it caused. You get three free take backs on every level. Since the deal never changes, you can try a cell, watch the chain, undo it and test another cell, which is a good way to learn how chains work.

### Do Honey Hive levels get harder as you go?

Gentle at first, then properly tough. Level 1 has 19 cells and two colors and can't be lost. Hard levels shrink the comb to 12-16 cells with six colors, and boss levels use up to seven. On a hard level, between about a third and two thirds of our computer test players get stuck on the first try, and easier levels always follow the hard ones.

### Is Honey Hive a hexa sort game?

Yes. It plays by the familiar hexa sort rules: three stacks offered at a time, matching tops merge, 10 of a color clear, and a full board ends the run. In Honey Hive, locked cells open only through play; each level's deal is fixed, so it is the same puzzle every try; and every level was won by our solver with no hints or rescues before it went in the game. If you enjoy sorting by color, Sweet Stacks is the next one to try.

## Fruit Tumble: the tap-to-blast fruit game

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/fruit-tumble-tap-to-blast/

Fruit Tumble is the classic tap-to-blast game in Puzzle Jar. Tap two or more touching fruit of the same kind and they pop; the fruit above drops down and new fruit falls in from the top of the crate. Each level sets goals, such as 15 apples and 15 oranges, and a number of moves. Reach every goal before the moves run out and you win. Big groups leave a fizz rocket, a coconut or a blender behind.

### How do you play Fruit Tumble?

Tap any group of two or more matching fruit that touch. The whole group pops, everything above it tumbles down to fill the space, and fresh fruit drops in from the top. Each tap that pops something uses one move. The goal counters at the top go down as you collect the fruit they show, and there are six kinds in all: strawberry, blueberry, lemon, apple, orange and plum.

### Does tapping a single fruit waste a move?

No. A fruit with no matching neighbor does nothing when you tap it, and your move count stays where it was. Only a tap that pops a group, or sets off a special, uses a move, so a slip of the finger on a lone fruit costs you nothing.

### How do you make a fizz rocket, a coconut and a blender?

By the size of the group you pop. 5 or 6 fruit leave a fizz rocket on the square you tapped; it clears its row or its column, lying the way the group was longer. 7 or 8 leave a coconut with a lit fuse, which blasts the 8 squares around it. 9 or more make a blender that clears every fruit of its kind. Fruit in a group big enough wears a small badge of the special it would make, so you can see it before you tap.

### What happens when two specials sit side by side?

Tap one and both go off together as a bigger blast. Two rockets fire along a whole row and a whole column at once. A rocket with a coconut clears three rows and three columns. Two coconuts clear a 5x5 square. A blender next to a rocket or coconut turns every fruit of its kind into that special and sets them all off, and two blenders clear the entire crate.

### How do you win and lose in Fruit Tumble?

You win the moment every goal at the top reaches zero, even with moves left over. You lose when the move counter hits zero with a goal still open. Levels give between 14 and 39 moves, and there is no clock, so a slow, thought-out tap is never punished.

### What do ice, jam jars, gaps and nets do?

They are the obstacles, added one at a time. Ice blocks (from level 4) break when you pop fruit right next to them; frosted ice with a steel band (from level 20) takes two hits. Jam jars (level 8) have to be brought down to the bottom row. Gaps (level 11) are holes in the crate where no fruit can sit. Netted fruit (level 14) can't be tapped or grouped until a fruit beside it pops and cuts the net.

### How do you get a jam jar down to the bottom?

Empty the squares underneath it. A jar only drops when the fruit below it is gone, so pop groups in the jar's own column, as low as you can, rather than groups next to it. Specials are safe to use here: blasts never break a jar, so a rocket running up the jar's column clears its path in one move.

### What is the best strategy in Fruit Tumble?

Spend moves on the goals, and grow groups before you pop them. Popping a pair of a fruit you don't need often breaks up a bigger group that would have made a special. Look for taps that will make two groups of the same fruit fall together. Our careful computer test player, which only looks two taps ahead, uses about half of a level's moves, so a little planning goes a long way.

### Is the fruit that falls into the crate random?

No, it is fixed for each level. The same tap on the same board always brings in the same fruit, so a level plays the same way every time you retry it, and nothing changes against you when you are close to winning. When no group is left, the fruit is mixed, and that is also the same every time. Our tests replay a saved winning line of taps for every level to prove it can be won with no help.

### Which tap does the Fruit Tumble hint suggest?

The tap our careful player would choose. It plays every possible tap two taps ahead, already knowing which fruit will fall in, and picks the one that does most for the goals. If you just pause for 6 seconds, the biggest group on the board starts to glow for free, without using a hint.

### What can I do when I run out of moves in Fruit Tumble?

Take a rescue: 5 more moves, up to twice on a level. A video you opt into can pay for the first one on a level; the second uses a rescue from your shared count. You can also take back your last tap and get its move back (three take backs are free on each level), try the level again, or go home.

### What is the difference between Fruit Tumble, Balloon Bunch and Tide Pool?

All three are tap-to-blast games where two or more touching pieces of one kind pop, but each moves differently. Fruit Tumble is the classic grid: fruit falls down, new fruit drops in from the top, and you have a set number of moves. Balloon Bunch turns gravity upside down: loose balloons float up, drift and bump, and fireworks join together when they touch. It also has a move limit. Tide Pool drops nothing in from the top. Every few taps the tide pushes a new row up from the bottom, and you lose by letting the pool overflow, not by running out of moves.

### Who will enjoy Fruit Tumble?

If you have played any collapse or blast puzzle where you tap groups of the same color, you will know the rules after one tap. It suits players who want quick, colorful levels with a bit of planning, rather than long thinking puzzles. Our version has no lives to wait for, and the hard levels are hard because of the board, not because the falling fruit turns against you.

## Balloon Bunch: the floating balloon pop game

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/balloon-bunch-pop-game/

Balloon Bunch is the tap-to-blast game in Puzzle Jar where the pieces float. Tap two or more touching balloons of one color to pop them; the balloons below drift up into the gap and new ones rise in from the bottom of the tent. Reach the goals at the top before your moves run out. A bunch of 5 or more leaves a firework, and fireworks that touch join into a bigger one by themselves.

### How do you play Balloon Bunch?

Tap a bunch: two or more balloons of the same color that touch. They pop, the ones under them float up to fill the space, and new balloons rise in from below. Each pop costs one move, and the counters at the top go down as you collect the colors they ask for. Every color wears its own picture (red heart, blue star, yellow smile, green clover, orange paw, purple moon), so you never have to tell colors apart by shade alone.

### Why do the balloons move around after I pop some?

Because they really float. The balloons are not locked in a grid: they rise, bump into each other and settle under the tent roof, much like real balloons. So a pop can push balloons into new bunches you didn't plan, for better or worse. A move ends when everything has stopped drifting, which takes a couple of seconds at most.

### How do fireworks work in Balloon Bunch?

Pop 5 to 7 balloons at once for a small firework, 8 to 10 for a medium one, 11 or more for a big one. The firework stays where you tapped the bunch. Tap it and it pops every balloon around it, reaching wider the bigger it is, and sets off any other firework it touches, all for a single move.

### What happens when two fireworks touch?

They join into one firework a size bigger, all on their own, as the balloons drift. Two small ones become a medium, and two mediums become a big one. This is the heart of the game: make two fireworks close to each other, let the floating bring them together, and you get a bigger blast without paying for it in extra pops.

### Should I always go for the biggest firework?

No. A big firework needs 11 balloons in one bunch, and chasing it can burn several moves on small pops. We measured a player that always taps the biggest bunch and sets off every firework straight away: it won only 6 of our 37 hard levels and 1 of 12 boss levels. Firework placement and timing matter more than size.

### How do you win and lose in Balloon Bunch?

Win by bringing every goal counter at the top to zero; lose if your moves run out first. Levels give between 12 and 34 moves. Tapping a balloon with no match beside it does nothing and uses no move, so there is no penalty for a stray tap.

### Where should I tap first in Balloon Bunch?

Think about what will rise into the gap. Balloons move up, so popping a bunch high in the tent pulls up everything under it, while a pop near the bottom only changes the lower rows and the new balloons coming in. Pop next to the clouds and tied balloons you need to clear, and pick bunches whose neighbors, once they float up, will form a bunch in a goal color.

### What are clouds and dark clouds?

Obstacles that sit in the tent and get in the balloons' way. A cloud (from level 4) breaks when balloons touching it pop; a dark cloud (from level 14) needs two hits. Because everything floats up, a cloud keeps the balloons beneath it from rising past, so breaking one often reshapes the board.

### What is a tied balloon?

A balloon wrapped in ribbon, from level 8. It can't be tapped and can't be part of a bunch until a balloon touching it pops and unties it. After that it plays like any other balloon of its color, so untying the ones in a goal color early gives you more to work with.

### How does the Balloon Bunch hint choose a tap?
