It shows the tap our careful player would make. To choose it, the game takes the seven taps that look best, plays each one out with the real floating, then tries the best four taps after each. If you wait 6 seconds without tapping, the biggest bunch on the board glows for free.

### What does a rescue give you in Balloon Bunch?

Five extra moves. Two are allowed per level, and one of them can be earned by watching a video instead of spending a rescue you own.

### Can you get through Balloon Bunch by tapping anything?

Only on the early levels. The balloons that rise in are the same on every try of a level, and when no bunch is left they swap colors the same way each time, so careful play is what gets you through, not luck.

### How tough are the boss levels in Balloon Bunch?

Tough by design: a boss comes every fourth hard level, and most players need more than one try or a rescue on them. If you win easily, the game moves you to a tougher level set. Levels come in rounds of easy, medium and hard, so a breather always follows. The start is gentle: level 1 asks for 14 blue stars in 31 moves and can't be lost.

## Tide Pool: the rising-rows blast puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/tide-pool-blast-puzzle/

Tide Pool is the tap-to-blast game in Puzzle Jar where the danger comes from below. Tap two or more touching sea creatures of one kind to pop them. Every few taps the tide pushes a new row up from the bottom of the pool, and if a column is pushed past the top, the level is lost. Reach the goals before that happens. There is no move limit and no clock: the tide only moves when you tap.

### How do you play Tide Pool?

Tap a group of two or more matching creatures that touch: red crabs, blue fish, yellow starfish, green turtles, orange shells or purple jellyfish. They pop, and the creatures above them drop down into the gap. Nothing new falls in from the top. Instead, a counter at the top left tells you how many taps are left before the tide pushes in the next row.

### When does the tide push a new row up?

After a set number of taps, shown as "Next row in" at the top of the screen. Level 1 is slow, with a new row every 5 taps; after that the tide comes every 3 taps, or every 2 on many levels. The incoming row is visible faintly through the water below the pool, so you always know which creatures are about to arrive.

### How do you lose in Tide Pool?

By overflow: the tide pushes in a row while some column already reaches the top of the pool. The top row turns red as a warning when any column is one row from the top. If there is nothing left to tap, rows keep coming in until there is, so an empty-looking board is not always safe either.

### How do you win a level of Tide Pool?

Finish every goal shown at the top, and the level ends right away. Early goals ask you to collect creatures of one or two kinds. From level 4 some levels ask you to ride out a number of rows instead, which means surviving while that many rows come in. Later levels add rocks to break as a goal too.

### How do waves work in Tide Pool?

Pop 5 or 6 creatures at once and a small wave is left where you tapped; it washes away its whole row. 7 or 8 make a medium wave, which takes its row and the one above. 9 or more make a big wave: its row, the one above and the one below. Tap a wave to set it off, and any wave it hits goes off too. Creatures in a group big enough wear a small wave badge before you tap.

### Where is the best place to make a wave?

Low in the pool. A wave washes away whole rows, and the bottom rows are the fullest, so a wave set off near the bottom clears more than the same wave near the top. Clearing a full row also lowers every column by one at once, which is exactly what keeps the tide from overflowing the pool.

### Should I pop small pairs in Tide Pool?

Only when you need to. Every tap moves the tide closer, and a pair clears just two creatures while the tide adds a whole row of 7 or 8. Bigger groups clear more per tap and can leave a wave. When the pool is nearly full, though, a quick pop that brings the tallest column down is worth more than waiting for a perfect group.

### What are rocks, mossy rocks and seaweed?

Rocks (from level 8) can't be tapped; they break when creatures right next to them pop, and mossy rocks (from level 20) take two hits. Seaweed (from level 14) wraps a creature so it can't be tapped or grouped until a creature beside it pops. Both can arrive with the rising rows, so check the waiting row for trouble before you tap.

### What does the Tide out rescue do?

The tide goes out and the bottom 4 rows drain away, giving the pool plenty of room again. The tide can be sent out twice per level, once for a video if you want it that way. Taps made before a rescue can't be taken back afterwards, so a rescue you have used can't be undone by mistake.

### What does a hint show in Tide Pool?

A ring around the exact square to tap. Our careful player picks it by playing every tap together with the best tap after it, already knowing which rows the tide will bring; it keeps the pool low, the goals moving and waves in hand for later. If you wait 6 seconds, the biggest group glows for free.

### Is Tide Pool timed like older rising-rows games?

No. In many classic rising-row games, new rows creep up on a clock, so speed matters. In Tide Pool the tide counts your taps, not seconds, which turns it into a thinking game: you can study the pool and the waiting row for as long as you like before each tap.

### Does Tide Pool get harder later on?

Level 1 is a 7 by 10 pool with four kinds of creature, a row every 5 taps and a goal of 12 fish; it can't be lost.

## Garland Tangle: the untangle puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/garland-tangle-rope-untangle/

Garland Tangle is the untangle puzzle in Puzzle Jar. Paper lanterns stand on wooden posts, joined by strings of lights. Move a lantern to an empty post, and every string that no longer crosses another one lights up. Light all the strings before your moves run out to win. There is no timer and there are no lives, only a count of moves.

### How do you play Garland Tangle?

Drag a lantern onto an empty post, or tap the lantern and then the post; either way, that is one move. The strings tied to the lantern follow it. A string that crosses no other string glows in its own color, while a crossed one stays dark on a red cord. The counter at the top shows how many crossings are left to undo.

### Why can't I put a lantern anywhere I like?

Lanterns only sit on posts, and only on empty ones. Most boards have one or two spare posts, so every move is really a choice of which lantern goes to which free post. Moving a lantern also frees the post it came from, and that spot is often exactly where the next lantern needs to go.

### How do you win and lose in Garland Tangle?

You win when every string is lit, meaning no two strings cross anywhere. You lose when the move counter reaches zero with a crossing still on the board. Levels give between 4 and 24 moves, while our solver needs only 1 to 7, so the limit leaves room for some wrong turns.

### How can I tell if two strings really cross?

Look at the cord color: a lit string crosses nothing, a dark one on a red cord crosses at least one other. We also place the posts well apart and never close to the line between two others, so a string never runs over a post it is not tied to. The cord color settles any near-touch for you.

### What is the best way to untangle the strings?

Don't just grab the move that removes the most crossings right now. We tested that greedy approach on every level: it wins most easy boards but none of the hard or boss boards. Instead, picture the finished, uncrossed shape first. Ask which lantern belongs on the outside and which in the middle, then work toward that picture, using the free post as a stepping stone.

### Which lantern should I move first?

Usually the one with the most strings. A lantern tied to three or four others needs a spot that can reach all of them without crossing, and there may be only one such post. A lantern with a single string fits almost anywhere, so place it last. Up to 4 strings can meet at one lantern on later boards.

### What are the steel lanterns?

Nailed lanterns, steel blue with a bolt through them, from level 8. They can't be moved at all. Treat them as fixed points: since the rest of the picture has to fit around them, they often tell you where the other lanterns must end up.

### What changes when a board has only one empty post?

The order of your moves starts to matter a lot. From level 14, medium and harder boards can have just one free post, so each move fills the only gap and opens a new one where the lantern used to be. It plays a little like a sliding puzzle: sometimes you move a lantern out of the way first just to open the right post.

### What does the ringed lantern and post mean?

It rings one lantern and one post: the first move of a short line that untangles the board. The game searches up to 12 moves ahead for it, and if that search comes up empty, it guides lanterns back to where the level's untangled picture has them, which always works. Wait 6 seconds without moving and the move that clears the most crossings is shown for free.

### What does a rescue give in Garland Tangle?

Four more moves, up to twice on a level. The first can be paid for with an optional video, the second with one of your shared rescues.

### Can I undo a lantern move?

Yes. Take back returns the last lantern to its old post and gives you the move back. The first three are free on every level. Trying a move, watching which strings light up, then taking it back is a fair way to explore a tricky board.

### How hard does Garland Tangle get?

Level 1 has 4 lanterns, 3 strings and one crossing, solved in one move out of the 16 it gives, and it can't be lost. Boards grow to 11 posts, 10 lanterns and 13 strings.

### Is Garland Tangle a good puzzle for adults who like logic?

Yes, especially if you enjoy seeing shapes in your head. It grew out of the old Planarity puzzle, where you drag points until no lines cross, which math fans have played for years. Each board is short, a handful of moves, and quiet: you think, move once, and watch the lights come on. It is less suited to anyone who wants fast action.

## Bubble Picnic: the bubble shooter

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/bubble-picnic-bubble-shooter/

Bubble Picnic is the bubble shooter in Puzzle Jar. Touch and slide to aim, then let go to shoot; when it lands in a touching group of three or more of its color, counting itself, they pop, and anything left hanging falls. Each level gives you a set number of bubbles and one goal: clear every bubble, or free the gold stars. There is no timer and no ceiling coming down on you.

### How do you aim in Bubble Picnic?

Touch the board and slide your finger. A dotted path shows the whole flight, bounces included, and a ring marks the exact spot where the bubble will stick. Let go to shoot. Bubbles bounce off the side walls, so you can bank a shot around a cluster that is in the way and reach a gap you could not hit straight on.

### When do bubbles pop and when do they fall?

Three or more touching bubbles of one color pop, counting the one you just shot. After the pop, every bubble that is no longer linked to the top of the field drops off the board. Falling bubbles count toward clearing the field just like popped ones, which is why cutting a thin link can be worth far more than a big pop.

### Can I swap the bubble I'm about to shoot?

Yes, and it's free. Tap the two bubbles at the bottom to switch the one in the shooter with the next one. You can always see both, so every shot is really a choice between two colors. Swapping costs no bubble and you can do it as often as you like.

### How do you get a rainbow bubble?

Clear 8 or more bubbles with one shot, adding the popped and the fallen together. Your next bubble then turns into a rainbow bubble, which counts as any color when it lands. Save it for a spot where it touches two different colored pairs, or where one pop will drop a big hanging cluster.

### How do you win and lose in Bubble Picnic?

Meet the level's goal, shown at the top and under the field, before your bubbles run out. Early levels ask you to clear every bubble; from level 4 many ask you to free the stars instead. A level gives between 8 and 45 bubbles. When the last one is shot and the goal isn't met, the level is lost.

### How do you free the stars?

A gold star caught in the field is freed when a pop touches it, or when it falls with the bubbles around it. The second way is often cheaper: instead of working through the bubbles next to a star, look for the link that holds its whole cluster to the top and break that. Star levels start with deeper fields, 5 to 8 rows, so there is usually no need to clear everything.

### What are stone bubbles?

Gray stones, from level 8, that never pop, whatever you hit them with. The only way to get rid of one is to make it fall, by clearing the bubbles that hold it to the top. When a stone sits in the middle of the field, plan your shots around the bubbles above it.

### What is the best strategy in Bubble Picnic?

Aim for drops, not just pops. Hitting the few bubbles that hold a big cluster up brings the whole thing down for one shot. Use the free swap to keep the color you will need next, and don't fire a bubble anywhere just to get rid of it: in our tests, stray shots that piled up were the main reason players ran out. Plain sensible play, always taking the shot that clears the most, still won about half of our hard levels.

### Are the bubble colors in Bubble Picnic random?

No. The colors you are given are set by the level and by what is still on the field, so the same level hands you the same bubbles each time you play it. Nothing is changed to make you lose. Each level has been beaten by our careful computer player, and its winning line of shots is saved as proof.

### What does a hint do in Bubble Picnic?

It draws the best shot in gold and rings the two bubbles at the bottom if you should swap first. Our careful player tries every spot it can reach with either bubble, plays out the best shot after each, and shows a straight shot instead of a bank shot when both do the same job. Pause for 6 seconds and the shot that clears the most right now is shown for free.

### What happens when Bubble Picnic runs out of bubbles?

Five more bubbles can be added to your shooter, two times per level at most; a video pays for one of those if you like, otherwise each costs a rescue. Another way out: undo the last shot, which returns that bubble to you, and on each level three of those undos cost nothing.

### Can I tell the bubbles apart without relying on color?

Yes. Every color carries its own white mark: a heart on red, a cloud on blue, a bolt on yellow, a clover on green, a daisy on orange and a moon on purple. You can play the whole game by shape alone, which helps players who find some colors hard to tell apart.

### How big do Bubble Picnic fields get?

Up to 9 bubbles wide and 13 rows deep, with as many as 6 colors. Level 1 is tiny by comparison: 2 rows and 3 colors, 13 bubbles to clear with 45 to shoot, and none of 400 computer test players lost it.

### Is Bubble Picnic like the classic bubble shooters?

Yes. If you grew up on arcade or flash bubble shooters, the aiming and bouncing will feel familiar. The difference is the pace: there is no timer and no ceiling pushing down, so every shot can be lined up calmly, and the challenge comes from having a fixed number of bubbles instead.

## Quilt Pins: the patchwork logic puzzle

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/quilt-pins-logic-puzzle/

Quilt Pins is the logic grid in Puzzle Jar. A square quilt is sewn from colored patches: put exactly one pin in every patch, one in every row and one in every column, and no two pins may touch, not even corner to corner. Every quilt has exactly one answer and can be solved by thinking alone, without guessing. A pin on a wrong square costs one of your 3 hearts.

### How do you play Quilt Pins?

Tap a square once to put a cross on it, your own note that no pin goes there. Tap it again to place a pin. Drag across several squares to cross them all at once. Squares that a placed pin already rules out show a faint dot, so you don't have to cross them by hand. When every patch, row and column has its pin, the quilt is finished.

### Is Quilt Pins the same as the Queens puzzle?

The rules are the same kind. Queens, the daily puzzle many people know from LinkedIn, and the older Star Battle puzzles all ask for one mark in every row, column and colored region, with no two touching. Quilt Pins is our own take: pins on a patchwork quilt instead of crowns, hearts for mistakes, and every quilt made by our own level maker. It has no connection to LinkedIn.

### What happens if I put a pin in the wrong square?

If the answer has no pin there, it counts as a mistake: the pin bounces off, the square is crossed out in red, and you lose a heart. A pin that would plainly break a rule, such as one in a row that already has a pin, simply won't go in and costs nothing. Lose all 3 hearts and you are stuck.

### Where should I start on a new quilt?

At the smallest patch, or at any patch that lies entirely inside one row or one column. A patch of a single square is a pin straight away. A patch that sits inside one row must take that row's pin, so you can cross out every other square of that row. Each pin you place then rules out its row, its column and the eight squares around it.

### What solving tricks does Quilt Pins use?

Five kinds of thinking, from plainest to hardest: A patch, row or column with only one square left must take its pin there. A patch whose free squares all lie in one row or column claims that line from every other patch. A square whose pin would leave some row, column or patch with no room at all can be crossed out. Groups: when two patches fit only in the same two rows, no other patch can use those rows (the same works with three). On the hardest quilts, a "what if" chain: imagine a pin, follow what it forces, and cross it out when it leads to a dead end.

### Do I ever have to guess in Quilt Pins?

No. Our solver checks every quilt before it goes in the game: each has exactly one answer, and that answer can be reached step by step with the kinds of thinking above. Even the "what if" chains on the hardest quilts are reasoning you can do in your head or with crosses. If you feel you must guess, there is a step you haven't spotted yet, and a hint will show it.

### How do the hearts work in Quilt Pins?

You start every level with 3 hearts, and each wrong pin costs one. Take back removes your last mistake and gives its heart back, though the square stays crossed out because you now know it is wrong. The first three take backs on a level are free. If all hearts are gone, a rescue gives you 3 more, up to twice on a level. There is no setting to switch hearts off.

### What does a hint do in Quilt Pins?

It places the next pin that can be worked out from the pins already on the quilt, and tells you why in plain words, such as which patch or row forced it. We did this because a hint that only shows the answer teaches nothing. Using hints well is a good way to learn the harder tricks.

### Is there a timer in Quilt Pins?

No clock is shown, and you can take as long as you like. The game does quietly note how long each quilt takes you: if you are slower than usual on 6 of your last 10 levels, the next quilts get a little smaller and easier. Two wins in a row without help nudge it the other way.

### How do Quilt Pins levels get harder?

They follow a fixed ladder. Levels 1 to 10 use small quilts from 4 by 4 up to 9 by 9; after that, quilts are 8 by 8 to 10 by 10. Levels 1 to 5 need only the plainest kind of thinking, and harder kinds arrive at levels 6, 21 and 51. From level 30, every tenth level is a "Hard" quilt, and levels 35, 45, 55 and so on bring an extra-big 11 by 11 "Boss".

### How many Quilt Pins puzzles are there?

Our bank holds 2,000 quilts, from 4 by 4 to 11 by 11, and each can be turned and mirrored 8 ways, so they play as 16,000 levels. You won't get the same quilt twice until a whole group of them has been used. On top of that there is a daily quilt in "Today's puzzles", drawn from a set of 60.

### Will I like Quilt Pins if I enjoy sudoku?

Very likely. It is the same pure deduction, one placement forcing the next, but with colored patches instead of numbers, so there is no arithmetic. Dark seams mark every patch border, so you can read the shapes even if you find some pastel colors hard to tell apart. It is the slowest, most thoughtful game in the jar, and it sits near the end of each lap of the level road for that reason.

## Route Duel: the route-clearing duel

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/route-duel-puzzle-duel/

Route Duel is the game Puzzle Jar grew from. You and a computer rival take turns launching routes off a board packed with them; a route can only leave if its path is clear, and it scores its length in cells. When the board is empty, whoever has more cells wins. It also has Solo Run, where you clear a board alone against a clock, the only timed mode in the whole app.

### How do you play Route Duel?

Tap a route whose head has a clear path off the board. It slides away, and every cell it covered is added to your score and colored in your color. Then the rival takes its turn. The bar at the top shows both scores and how many cells are still left on the board, so you always know how close the duel is.

### What happens if I tap a blocked route?

It bumps into whatever is in its way and you lose your turn, so the rival moves next. The route stays where it was. Before tapping, follow the route's path to the edge of the board with your eye: one cell of another route in the way is enough to block it.

### Is the Route Duel rival a real person?

No. The rival is always the computer, playing on your phone. Names such as Tyler or Emma are just names, picked at random for each new level; a retry of the same level keeps the same name, like a rematch. There is no online play against other people in Puzzle Jar.

### How do you win a Route Duel level?

Finish with more cells than the rival once the board is cleared. A lost duel doesn't move you on: you need to win the level to reach the next picture, even if you only lose by a few cells. A level 1 guided duel teaches the rules and can't be lost.

### What is the best strategy in Route Duel?

Look at what each launch frees, not just how long it is. Taking a route away can open the path of another route, and if that one is long, the rival gets it next turn. A shorter route that frees nothing is often better than a long one that hands over a bigger prize. Late in a duel, count the cells left: sometimes you only need to stay ahead, not score big.

### Does the Route Duel rival get stronger or weaker?

Both, depending on how you play. It adjusts to you: if you are struggling, it plays a little weaker, and if you are winning easily, a little stronger. Each level also has its own rival strength, shown under the level title, such as "Medium rival".

### What is Solo Run in Route Duel?

A timed mode with no rival. You clear a tightly packed picture board on your own before the clock runs out, allowing about 4 seconds a route and never less than 2 minutes. A blocked tap costs 5 seconds. Once per run, when time is up, you can watch a video for 60 more seconds. Solo Run opens once you reach Route Duel level 6, and its button sits on Route Duel's card in Free play.

### Is there a time limit in Route Duel duels?

No. Normal duels have no clock at all; you can think as long as you like before each launch. The clock belongs only to Solo Run, which you choose to play. It is the one countdown anywhere in Puzzle Jar's 20 games.

### What are the picture boards in Route Duel?

Each level after the first is a picture, such as a cat, filled with our own routes. The outlines come from Google's Noto Emoji pictures (credited in Settings). There are 340 of them after the guided first duel, 341 levels in all. As the routes leave, the picture fills in with your color and the rival's.

### What do hints and take backs do in Route Duel?

A hint makes your best route glow, the one our solver would launch now. Take back undoes your last move, so you can try a different route if your launch freed something big for the rival. Both come from the shared counts used by every game in the app, and the first three take backs on each level are free. Solo Run has no take back.

### What happens when I lose a duel?

The level plays again, or you can use a rescue. A rescue takes you back a few moves against a tired rival that plays weaker, so you can win from a position you already reached. Each time you lose, the result card lets you pay for a rescue with a short video you choose to watch or with one of your shared rescues.

### How hard does Route Duel get?

Levels come in rounds of easy, medium and hard, with every fourth hard level a boss and an easy level after each hard one. Big pictures with many routes take more planning.

### Why is Route Duel the last game on the level road?

Because it is one of the two hardest, together with Quilt Pins, and the road saves them for the end of each lap through the 20 games. It is also where the app began: Puzzle Jar was called Route Duel before it grew into a collection, and players kept their levels when it changed.

## Is Puzzle Jar free? Ads, purchases and prices

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/is-puzzle-jar-free/

Yes. Puzzle Jar is free to download, all 20 games are open from the first launch, and every level can be won without spending anything. The app is paid for by full-screen ads between levels, starting after your 3rd finished level, each one announced by a 5-second "Ad loading" card. A one-time Remove Ads purchase ($5.99 in the US) turns them off for good, and small packs of hints, take backs and rescues are for sale.

### Is Puzzle Jar free?

Yes, free to download on iPhone and Android, with nothing locked. You get all 20 games, the daily puzzles and the full level road without paying. There is no subscription and no trial that runs out. The game earns money in two ways: ads between levels, and optional purchases such as Remove Ads and helper packs. You can play for months and never open the shop.

### Why does Puzzle Jar have ads?

Because the ads are what keep the game free. We are a small studio, and most players never buy anything, so the ads between levels pay for the new games and levels we keep adding. We chose ads over a paywall or a waiting timer: there is never a clock standing between you and the next level. If ads bother you, one purchase removes them instead of a monthly fee.

### When do ads start in Puzzle Jar?

At the end of your third finished level. The first two levels you finish, in any of the 20 games, never show a full-screen ad, so you can try the app properly first. On iPhone, the app also asks Apple's "Allow tracking?" question at the very first launch, before any ad is loaded. From the end of that third level on, an ad can appear whenever a level ends.

### How often do ads show between levels?

Once 3 levels are finished, a full-screen ad can come at the end of any level, won or lost, when you tap to go on. There are two breaks: no full-screen ad comes within 20 seconds of a rewarded video you chose to watch, and none comes if no ad has loaded yet. In that second case you simply go on to the next screen without an ad.

### Are there ads in the middle of a level?

No. A level is never stopped by an ad. Full-screen ads only appear after a level is over, on the way to the next one or back home. If you leave a level halfway through with the back button, no ad plays at all. The only videos you can see during play are rewarded ones that you start yourself by tapping a "watch ad" button.

### Does Puzzle Jar have banner ads?

No. There are no banner ads anywhere in Puzzle Jar: not along the bottom of the board, not on the Home screen, not in Settings. The board always has the whole screen. The only ads are the full-screen ones between levels and the rewarded videos you pick yourself.

### What is the 5-second "Ad loading" screen?

It is a warning card we show before every full-screen ad. It counts down from 5, so an ad never jumps out at you in the middle of a tap. On the card is a REMOVE ADS button with the price in your currency. If you ignore it, the countdown ends and the ad plays; if you buy, the ad is dropped there and then.

### What do rewarded videos give you?

One helper each time you watch to the end. On the offer sheet a video gives +1 hint, +1 take back or +1 rescue, whichever you asked for. In most games the first rescue of a level can be paid with a video. In Solo Run one video a run adds 60 seconds to the clock, and on Home a video can save a broken day streak of 2 days or more, that day or the next.

### Do I have to watch rewarded videos?

No, they are always your choice. A rewarded video only starts when you tap a button that says "watch ad", and saying "NOT NOW" costs nothing. If you close a video early you just don't get that reward. Nothing in the game, not a level, a game or a feature, is locked until you watch one.

### How much does Remove Ads cost?

$5.99 in the US, paid once. It is not a subscription: you buy it once and keep it, and it comes back on a new phone through Restore purchases. Outside the US the App Store or Google Play shows its own price in your currency, which can be higher or lower than the US figure.

### What does Remove Ads remove?

It removes every full-screen ad between levels, in all 20 games, along with the 5-second "Ad loading" card. What stays are the rewarded videos, because those are a way to earn free helpers: the "watch ad" buttons are still there if you want a free hint or rescue, and they never play by themselves. We think that is fairer than taking the free option away from paying players.

### What else do you get with Remove Ads?

Unlimited take backs. Normally the first 3 take backs on each level are free and later ones come from your count; with Remove Ads every take back is free, and the button shows an infinity mark instead of a number. We added this because a common complaint about puzzle games is that paying to remove ads still leaves undoing a slip behind a paywall. Hints and rescues still come from their counts.

### How do I remove ads from Puzzle Jar?

Buy Remove Ads in one of two places. On the 5-second "Ad loading" card, tap REMOVE ADS. Or open Settings with the button next to the name on the Home screen and tap "Remove ads", which shows the price. Apple or Google then asks you to confirm. Once it goes through, the Settings button says ads are removed, and the "Ad loading" card never appears again.

### Can I get rid of ads without paying?

Not with a switch, but playing with no internet stops most of them. Full-screen ads have to download before they can play, so in airplane mode they mostly cannot load and the level ends without one. An ad that loaded before you went offline can still show once. The catch: rewarded videos need internet too, so offline you cannot earn free helpers that way. More on this on our offline play page .

### What can you buy in Puzzle Jar?

Seven things. These are the US prices; your store shows your own currency. Item US price Kind Remove Ads (plus unlimited take backs) $5.99 One-time, kept for good Starter Pack: Remove Ads, 30 hints, 5 rescues $2.99 One-time, offered once (only shown when your store can sell it) 10 Hints $0.99 Pack, used up 60 Hints $4.99 Pack, used up 150 Hints (marked "BEST VALUE") $9.99 Pack, used up 30 Take Backs $0.99 Pack, used up 5 Rescues $0.99 Pack, used up

### Why are Puzzle Jar's prices different in my country?

Because each store sells in local currency. The App Store and Google Play turn a price into your currency using their own price points, and in many countries that price includes sales tax or VAT, so it rarely matches the US figure after exchange. The game shows the price your store gives it, so the number on a button is the store's price for your account. The US prices on this page are only a guide.

### What is the Starter Pack?

A one-time deal: Remove Ads, 30 hints and 5 rescues for $2.99 in the US, less than Remove Ads costs on its own. It appears once, on the Home screen, after you win level 21 of the level road. From the moment you first see it, it stays on sale for 48 hours, with a small timer on Home. It is never shown to anyone who already owns Remove Ads.

### Can I still get the Starter Pack after it ends?

No. When its 48 hours run out, the Starter Pack is gone for good and does not come back later. We did it this way so the offer is honest: a one-time deal that really is one-time, instead of a "last chance" that returns every week. Remove Ads and all the helper packs stay on sale at their normal prices.

### Is Puzzle Jar pay to win?

No. Puzzle Jar has no scores against other people, no rankings and no levels that need a purchase. Hints and rescues make a hard level quicker, but they are never required: you can retry a level as often as you like at no cost. A player who never pays sees exactly the same levels as one who buys everything.

### Can every level be beaten without paying?

Yes. Money buys speed in Puzzle Jar, never access: helpers save you tries, but nothing you can buy opens a level, adds a level or changes how a level is built. A player who has spent nothing has every move a paying player has. A hard level may take several tries; it never takes a purchase. How we prove each level can be won is on our stuck and difficulty page .

### Are any games or levels locked behind a purchase?

No. All 20 games are open in Free play from the first launch, and the level road and daily puzzles cost nothing. The only thing in the app that unlocks by playing is Solo Run, the timed mode inside Route Duel, which opens at Route Duel level 6. Nothing can be unlocked early with money.

### Does Puzzle Jar have coins or gems?

No. There is no coin, gem or other in-game money to earn, collect or buy. Every price in the shop is in real money, shown in your own currency, and each pack says plainly what it gives, such as "10 hints". We left out an in-game currency on purpose, so you never have to work out what a bundle of gems is really worth.

### Does Puzzle Jar have lives or energy?

No. There are no lives, no energy bar and no waiting to play. Lose a level and you can tap TRY AGAIN, as many times as you want, for free; the only thing that may come first is a full-screen ad, unless you own Remove Ads. A few games, such as Quilt Pins and Pencil Case, have 3 hearts inside a single level, but losing them only ends that try.

### Which hint pack is the best value?

The 150-hint pack, if you use hints often. In the US it costs $9.99, about 6.7 cents a hint, against 9.9 cents in the 10-hint pack and about 8.3 cents in the 60-hint pack. If you only want a few for one stuck level, the $0.99 pack is the cheaper buy overall. Before you buy, remember the free supply: a full jar on Home gives +1 hint, and a rewarded video gives +1.

### Do hints, take backs and rescues expire?

No, they have no expiry date. A hint bought today still works in a year, in any of the 20 games. There is one catch: helper counts are saved only on your phone. If you delete the app or move to a new phone, unused hints, take backs and rescues are lost, and Restore purchases cannot bring packs back because each pack is used up as you spend it.

### How do I restore purchases in Puzzle Jar?

Open Settings from the Home screen and tap "Restore purchases". You need internet and the same Apple ID or Google account you bought with. Restore brings back one-time purchases: Remove Ads, the Remove Ads part of the Starter Pack, and the old unlimited hints or take backs from Route Duel. It does not refill used or lost packs of hints, take backs or rescues.

### Why do I still see ads after buying Remove Ads?

First, check which kind of ad it is. Rewarded videos stay after the purchase, but they only play when you tap a "watch ad" button. If a full-screen ad or the "Ad loading" card still appears on its own, the purchase has not reached the game: open Settings, tap "Restore purchases" while online, and make sure the phone is signed in to the account that paid. If it still happens, email us at sultanofniyyat@gmail.com.

### How do I get a refund for a Puzzle Jar purchase?

Ask the store you paid, because Apple and Google handle every payment and we never see your card. On iPhone, go to reportaproblem.apple.com , sign in, find the purchase and choose to request a refund. On Android, start from Google Play's refund policy help page , which links to the request steps. The store decides; we cannot issue refunds ourselves.

### What if an ad in Puzzle Jar looks misleading or inappropriate?

Please tell us. The ads come from Google's AdMob network, so we do not make or pick each one, but AdMob lets us block an advertiser or a whole category once we know about it. Email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with what the ad showed, which app or game it was for, and roughly when you saw it. A screenshot helps.

### Does every Puzzle Jar purchase go through Apple or Google?

Yes. Every purchase opens the App Store's or Google Play's own payment sheet, and nothing is charged until you confirm it there. Depending on your store settings, that step can also ask for a password, Face ID or fingerprint. That also means the store's family settings apply, such as Ask to Buy; our kids and safety page explains them for parents.

### I bought unlimited hints in Route Duel. Do I still have them?

Yes. Puzzle Jar grew out of Route Duel, and the old "unlimited hints" and "unlimited take backs" purchases are still honored in all 20 games. They are no longer sold, but if you own one, hints or take backs show an infinity mark and cost nothing. On a new phone, Restore purchases brings them back like Remove Ads.

### Are there cheats or promo codes for Puzzle Jar?

No. There are no cheat codes, and the game has no box to type a code into. Sites that offer "free hint generators" for puzzle games are not connected to us and cannot add anything to your phone; avoid giving them your details. The free ways to get helpers are the real ones: fill the jar with 10 wins for one hint, one take back and one rescue, or watch an optional video for one more.

## Playing Puzzle Jar offline, with no wifi

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/offline-puzzle-games-no-wifi/

Yes, Puzzle Jar plays fully offline. All 20 games, every level and the daily puzzles are stored inside the app, so they work in airplane mode, underground or anywhere with no signal. Only ads, purchases, Restore purchases and the privacy questions need internet, and your progress saves on the phone either way.

### Can you play Puzzle Jar without wifi?

Yes. Puzzle Jar needs no wifi and no mobile data to play. The levels are built into the app when you download it, so nothing has to come from the internet when you start a level. You can open the app with the phone in airplane mode and play the level road, Free play or today's puzzles exactly as you would at home.

### Do all 20 games work offline?

Yes, every one of them, from Bolts & Jars to Route Duel. None of the 20 games has an online-only mode, a live event or a level that streams in. Route Duel's rival is played by the phone itself, not by another person over the internet, so even the duel works on a plane.

### What in Puzzle Jar needs an internet connection?

Four things, none of them needed to play: Ads: full-screen ads between levels and the rewarded videos you choose. Buying anything, and the prices in your currency. Restore purchases, which asks Apple or Google what you own. Google's privacy form in Europe and the UK, and changing your Privacy choices. The Starter Pack card is also only shown when the store can be reached.

### Does Puzzle Jar use mobile data?

Mostly for ads. A level itself needs no data, but if mobile data is on, the app downloads ads in the background and fetches store prices, and on Android it also sends small Google Analytics notes, such as a won level. We have not measured how many megabytes that adds up to, so we won't quote a number. Video ads are usually the biggest part, so if your plan is tight, the next answer shows how to switch data off for the app alone.

### How do I stop Puzzle Jar using mobile data?

Turn mobile data off for this one app. On iPhone: Settings, then Mobile Data (Cellular in the US), scroll to Puzzle Jar and switch it off. On Android, open Settings, find Puzzle Jar under Apps, then its mobile data or data usage entry, and turn off mobile data use; the exact names differ by phone maker. The game keeps working on mobile; ads and purchases wait for wifi.

### Can I play Puzzle Jar in airplane mode?

Yes. Airplane mode only cuts the connection, and the game does not need one. Your levels, the jar on Home, your helper counts and your day streak all keep working. With the connection off, most full-screen ads cannot load, and you won't be able to buy anything or watch a rewarded video until you are back online.

### Is Puzzle Jar a good game for a long flight?

It suits one well: one download gives you 20 games that never ask for wifi. You can stop at any moment for landing or a meal cart, since there is no clock in 19 of the 20 games, and a level left halfway simply starts again later. Bring headphones or turn the sound off in Settings. If you want a wider list for travel, see our best puzzle games guide .

### Can I play Puzzle Jar underground or with a patchy signal?

Yes, and a weak signal does not freeze the board. The levels never wait on the network. The only things that try to use the connection are ads and the store, and if no ad has finished loading when a level ends, you go on without one, sometimes after a short pause (never more than about 15 seconds) while the app tries to reach the ad network. Rewarded video buttons may say the ad isn't ready yet; try again once you have signal.

### Are the daily puzzles available offline?

Yes. "Today's puzzles" are already inside the app, one for each game, picked by the date on your phone from puzzles we shipped with it. Nothing is downloaded each morning, so a new set is ready after midnight even with no signal. Solving them offline still fills your jar and keeps your day streak going.

### Does my progress save when I play offline?

Yes. Progress is always written to the phone itself, online or not, the moment a level ends: your road level, each game's own level, the jar, the day streak and your helpers. There is no server copy to sync later, so you lose nothing by playing for a week without a connection.

### Do rewarded videos work offline?

No. A rewarded video has to download from Google's ad network before it can play, so with no internet the "watch ad" buttons cannot give a free hint, take back, rescue or extra Solo Run time. The game tells you the ad isn't ready rather than pretending. Hints, take backs and rescues you already have still work as normal.

### Can I use hints offline?

Yes, any hints, take backs and rescues you have saved work with no connection, and the 3 free take backs on each level do too. What you can't do offline is top up: buying a pack and watching a video for +1 both need internet. One top-up does work offline: every full jar on Home still gives +1 hint, +1 take back and +1 rescue.

### Does Remove Ads still work when I'm offline?

Yes. Once you own Remove Ads, the game remembers it on the phone, so it never has to check with Apple or Google before each level. Your unlimited take backs keep working offline too. Only on a new phone or after reinstalling do you need a connection once, to tap Restore purchases in Settings.

### Can I buy hints or restore purchases offline?

No. Every purchase and every Restore goes through the App Store or Google Play, which need a connection. Offline, Restore purchases answers "Couldn't reach the App Store" or "Couldn't reach Google Play", and no money is taken. Wait until you have signal and try again; nothing is lost by waiting.

### What happens when I go back online?

Very little, and that's on purpose. Your progress is already on the phone, so there is nothing to upload or merge. Ads start loading again, so a full-screen ad can follow the next level once one has arrived, and the shop shows prices in your currency again. If a purchase was interrupted by losing signal, the store usually finishes it the next time the app opens online.

### Should I download Puzzle Jar before a trip?

Yes, on wifi, before you leave. The iPhone download is about 106 MB, so it is better done at home than on airport wifi. Then open the app once while you are still online and answer its first-launch questions, play a level, and you're set. If you want Remove Ads or a hint pack for the trip, buy it before you go, because the shop needs a connection.

### What happens if I open Puzzle Jar for the first time with no internet?

It still starts. On the first launch the app asks its privacy questions: Apple's tracking question on iPhone, plus Google's consent form in Europe and the UK. Google's form needs a connection, so offline it is skipped and asked again later. The game never waits longer than 15 seconds for those questions before letting you play, and every level works from the start.

### Does Puzzle Jar drain the battery?

We haven't measured battery use, so we can't give hours or percentages. What we can tell you: the game draws at most 60 frames a second, and it never needs the network to run a level. For a long day away from a charger, lower the screen brightness and use airplane mode, which also stops ads from downloading in the background.

### Does the day streak work offline?

Yes. The streak counts each day in a row on which you finish a level in any game, using the phone's own date, so a week of offline play keeps it alive. The one part that needs internet is saving a broken streak: that uses a rewarded video, which can't play without a connection. You can do it that day or the next once you have signal.

### Does Solo Run work offline?

Yes. Solo Run, the timed mode inside Route Duel, has its boards stored in the app like every other level, and its clock runs on the phone. The only part you lose offline is the once-a-run rewarded video that adds 60 seconds, since that video has to download first. Solo Run opens after Route Duel's first 5 levels.

### Do I need internet to get new levels?

No. Every level the game will give you is already in the app. Most games have 150 levels on the road, in three level sets, and after level 150 a game carries on by replaying from its level 51; Quilt Pins picks from a bank of 2,000 quilts. New games or levels arrive only through an app update from the App Store or Google Play.

### Can an ad still show when I'm offline?

Sometimes, yes. The app loads the next ad ahead of time, so if one finished downloading before you lost signal, it can still play after a level, once. After that no new ad can arrive until you are back online. We say this plainly because "turn on airplane mode" is often given as a way to stop ads completely, and that isn't quite true.

### Can I play Puzzle Jar abroad without paying for roaming?

Yes. Switch off data roaming, or the whole connection, and the game carries on exactly the same, so you are never charged abroad just to play. Your progress stays on the phone, and you can return to wifi at the hotel whenever you like to restore purchases or watch a rewarded video for a free helper.

### Does offline play work the same on Android and iPhone?

Yes. The iPhone and Android versions hold the same levels and play the same games, and both save to the phone. The one difference is the first-launch privacy question: on iPhone it is Apple's "Allow tracking?" box, which does not need a connection, while Google's consent form for Europe and the UK needs internet on both phones.

### Why do some "offline" puzzle games still need internet?

Usually because they load something from a server before a level can start: an ad that has to play first, an energy timer checked online, a live event, or levels that download as you reach them. When the server can't be reached, the game stops or keeps asking for wifi. We built Puzzle Jar the other way round: levels ship inside the app, and an ad that can't load is simply left out, so no server has to answer before you can play.

### Does the jar fill when I play offline?

Yes. Every win in any game drops a piece into the jar on Home, online or offline, and 10 pieces fill it. A full jar gives +1 hint, +1 take back and +1 rescue for any game, then a fresh jar begins. It is the only way to earn free helpers without a connection, which makes it handy on a long trip.

## Stuck on a level: hints, take backs, rescues and difficulty

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/stuck-hints-and-difficulty/

Every Puzzle Jar level can be won with no help: a computer solver beats each one before it ships. When you are stuck you have three helpers shared by all 20 games: a hint shows a safe move, a take back undoes your last move (3 free on every level), and a rescue gives you a little extra room after you get stuck. New players start with 3 hints, 3 take backs and 1 rescue, and losing a level never costs anything.

### What are hints, take backs and rescues?

They are the three helpers in Puzzle Jar, each with its own count. A hint lights up a good next move, worked out by the game's solver. A take back puts your last move back. A rescue is the "so close" save once you're stuck: an extra tray hole, jar, shelf, a few more moves or hearts, depending on the game. Each game's own page says what its hint and rescue do.

### How many hints do you start with?

Three hints, plus 3 take backs and 1 rescue, as a welcome gift on your first launch. That is enough to try each helper before you ever need more. On top of that, the first 3 take backs on every level are free and do not touch your count, so your saved take backs are only used from the fourth one on a level.

### Is there a limit on hints per level?

No. You can use as many hints on one level as you have in your count, one at a time. Each hint shows only the next safe move, not the whole answer, so on a long level you may want several. Hints are shared by all 20 games, so the count you see in Sweet Stacks is the same one you'll spend in Honey Hive.

### How do take backs work in Puzzle Jar?

Each take back undoes one move, and the first 3 on every level are free. The button shows "3 FREE", then "2 FREE" and so on; after that each take back comes from your count. The free three reset on every new level and every retry. Sweet Stacks goes further: its undo and restart are always free. With Remove Ads, take backs cost nothing in every game.

### What is a rescue in Puzzle Jar?

A rescue is a second chance that appears on the stuck screen when a level is almost lost. It changes the board just enough to carry on: in Bolts & Jars a tray hole, in Bead Swap 5 extra moves, in Quilt Pins 3 more hearts, in Route Duel a replay from a few moves back against a weaker rival. In every game except Route Duel you keep all the progress you made before getting stuck.

### How many rescues can I use on one level?

Two in most games, one in four of them. Sweet Stacks, Nut Sort, Pencil Case and Shelf Sort allow a single rescue a level, because their rescue (an extra jar, bolt, refilled hearts or shelf) is strong enough to turn almost any position around. In the other games a second rescue is allowed. Past the cap, the stuck screen offers a take back, TRY AGAIN and HOME instead.

### Is the first rescue on a level free?

In most games it can be, if you watch a short video. The stuck screen offers the first rescue of a level for a rewarded video, and a second one from your rescue count. You never have to take the video: you can pay with a rescue you own instead, or skip the rescue and start the level again for free.

### How do I get more hints for free?

Two ways, both without paying. Keep winning, because wins fill the jar on the Home screen, which pays out one of each helper (more on the jar below). Or watch a rewarded video from the offer sheet, which gives +1 of the helper you asked for. Today's puzzles count as wins for the jar too, so the dailies help fill it.

### What happens when I run out of hints?

An offer sheet opens, the same in every game. It lists the packs for that helper with prices in your currency, a "WATCH AD" button for one free, and "NOT NOW". Choosing NOT NOW closes the sheet and returns you to the board as it was; nothing is lost and the level carries on without the hint.

### What does "WATCH AD · +1" mean?

It means one short video gives you one of the helper you were trying to use: one hint, one take back or one rescue. You get it only if the video plays to the end; closing it early gives nothing and costs nothing. The helper goes into your shared count, so you can spend it in this game or any other. Videos need an internet connection.

### What is the jar on the Puzzle Jar home screen?

It's a progress jar that fills as you win. Every win in any of the 20 games drops a piece into it in that game's color, and the next road level is shown beside it. When 10 pieces are in, the jar is full: you get one hint, one take back and one rescue for any game, and a fresh, empty jar starts.

### Are Puzzle Jar levels rigged to make you pay?

No. Each level is fixed: the same pieces, colors and order every time you play it, and in games where new pieces fall in, the order they fall is set for that level too. Nothing changes when you are close to winning, and the game never deals a worse board because you have hints or money to spend. If a level beat you, the same level, unchanged, is waiting when you retry.

### Is every Puzzle Jar level possible to win?

Yes. We run a solver over each level before it goes in the app, and it must finish the level with zero helpers. Levels the solver cannot clear are rebuilt or dropped. Quilt Pins goes one step further: every quilt has exactly one answer that can be reached by thinking alone, with no guessing.

### Does the game get harder if I keep winning?

Yes, a little. Puzzle Jar follows how you play, which we call the dial. Two clean wins in a row, with no retry and no hint or rescue, move you a step harder. In 18 games that means the next levels come from a tougher set of the same level numbers; Quilt Pins moves up its own ladder, and in Route Duel the rival plays stronger.

### Does Puzzle Jar get easier if I keep losing?

Yes. A win that needed a retry or a rescue moves the dial a step easier, so the next level comes from a gentler set. It goes back up once you string clean wins together again. In Route Duel, losing a duel makes the computer rival play weaker. The level you are stuck on itself never changes, though: the dial only picks the next one.

### Why does the first level of the day feel easier?

Because it is, by one step. The first new level you play each day is chosen one step gentler than your dial would otherwise pick, so you start the day with a win in reach rather than a wall. From the second level on, the dial goes back to its normal setting.

### What are easy, medium and hard rounds?

Levels come in rounds of three: easy, medium, hard. On the level road you play one round of a game, then move to the next game, round and round through all 20. An easy level always follows a hard one, so a tough level is followed by a breather. Levels 1 to 5 of each game are only easy or medium.

### What is a boss level?

Every fourth hard level is a boss: the toughest level of its stretch in that game, and in some games the place where a new obstacle shows up at its strongest. When you beat it, the win screen says "Boss beaten". A boss sits at the end of a round, so the next level is always an easy one.

### Does a level change when I retry it?

No. Once a level number has been picked for you, it stays the same level until you move past it, however many times you retry. You can learn it, plan from the first move and use what went wrong last time. The dial only adjusts the levels after the one you are on.

### What should I do when a level feels impossible?

Try these in order: Use your 3 free take backs to go back to the last point where you had choices. Start again and watch the first few moves; most hard levels are lost early, not at the end. Take one hint to see a safe move, then carry on yourself. Take a break: play the day's puzzles or another game in Free play and come back. Every level has a winning path, and retries are free.

### Can I skip a level in Puzzle Jar?

No, there is no skip button. A level on the road has to be won before the road moves on. When you are stuck, the stuck screen offers a rescue (while one is still allowed on that level), a take back, TRY AGAIN and HOME. You don't have to stay on it, though: every game is open in Free play, so you can play something else and come back.

### Can I play a different game when I'm stuck?

Yes. Go HOME and pick any of the 20 games from Free play; they are all open from the first launch. Free play moves that game's own level forward, while your road level waits where you left it. Wins in Free play still fill the jar, which can give you a free hint for the level you were stuck on.

### Does Puzzle Jar get harder forever?

No, it levels off. In 18 of the games, levels grow over the first 150 on the road, adding pieces, colors and obstacles at set points; after level 150 such a game carries on by replaying from its level 51, so the difficulty settles in its middle and hard range instead of climbing without end. Quilt Pins draws from a bank of 2,000 quilts, and Route Duel has 340 picture boards.

### What happens when I fail a level?

Nothing is taken from you. There are no lives to lose, no coins and no timer before you can play again. The stuck screen offers a rescue where one is allowed, TRY AGAIN to replay the same level from the start, or HOME. A full-screen ad may come before the next screen once you have finished 3 levels, unless you own Remove Ads.

### Can you lose level 1?

No. Level 1 of every game is a guided level that cannot be lost: a glow shows you where to tap while you learn the rules. In Route Duel, level 1 is a guided first duel. Losing becomes possible from level 2, and even then the first five levels of each game are only easy or medium.

### Do hints make the next level harder?

No. A win with a hint or a rescue is not counted as a clean win, so it never moves the dial toward harder levels. A rescue or a retry actually moves it a step easier. Take backs don't count against you at all, since three a level are free. Use helpers when you want; the game won't punish you for it.

### Why is one game in Puzzle Jar harder than another?

Because each game keeps its own dial. If you breeze through Hop On but struggle in Bead Swap, Hop On moves to its tougher levels while Bead Swap moves to gentler ones. The road also saves the two thinking-heaviest games, Quilt Pins and Route Duel, for last in each lap. Our puzzle types page explains what each kind of game asks of you.

### Is there a walkthrough or answer list for Puzzle Jar levels?

No, and a fixed list would not help much. In 18 of the games each level is picked from a normal, gentler or tougher set depending on how you have been playing, so your level 40 may not be the same board as a friend's level 40. The hint button is the walkthrough: it shows a safe next move worked out by the same solver that checked the level before release, on exactly the board you are looking at.

## Kids, families, safety and privacy

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/kids-safety-and-privacy/

Puzzle Jar is a calm, general-audience puzzle app with no chat, no strangers and no account. It is rated 4+ on the App Store and Everyone on Google Play, but it is not a kids' app: it shows ads from Google AdMob and offers in-app purchases, which parents can lock with the store's own settings. We ask for no name, email or photos; Google collects device data for ads, and on Android the game also uses Google Analytics for Firebase.

### What age rating does Puzzle Jar have?

4+ on the App Store and Everyone on Google Play. The games have no violence, scary content, gambling or rude words: you sort colors, match shapes and untangle strings. The rating covers what is inside the game. It does not cover the ads, which come from Google's ad network, or the in-app purchases, which the store pages also list.

### Is Puzzle Jar safe for kids?

The games themselves are, and there is no way for a child to talk to anyone. But Puzzle Jar is made for a general audience, not as a children's app. It shows ads between levels and has in-app purchases, so for a young child we suggest turning on the store's purchase protection and, if ads are a worry, buying Remove Ads or letting them play offline. Our privacy policy says plainly that the app is not directed at children under 13.

### Can kids chat with strangers in Puzzle Jar?

No. Puzzle Jar has no chat, no messages, no friends list, no profiles and no online play with other people. Route Duel's rival is the computer, played by the phone itself. Nobody can see what your child is doing in the game or contact them through it.

### Can kids make in-app purchases by accident?

Not without the store's own confirm step. Every purchase opens Apple's or Google's own payment sheet, and nothing is charged until someone confirms it there. Whether that step also asks for a password, Face ID or fingerprint depends on the phone's store settings, and a phone that recently passed a check may not ask again. That is why the settings below are worth turning on.

### How do I turn on Ask to Buy on iPhone?

Ask to Buy is part of Apple's Family Sharing. The family organizer turns it on for a child's account in the Family part of iPhone Settings. After that, when the child taps a purchase in any app, Puzzle Jar included, a request goes to the parent's phone to approve or decline. Screen Time's content restrictions can also block in-app purchases altogether.

### How do I require a password for purchases on Google Play?

In the Google Play app, open Settings from your profile picture, go to the authentication section and set purchases to need authentication every time. Play then asks for your password or fingerprint before each purchase. Parents can also manage a child's account with Google Family Link.

### What kind of ads might my child see in Puzzle Jar?

Ads chosen by Google's AdMob network, often for other apps and games. We do not make or hand-pick them, so we can't promise every one suits a young child. Full-screen ads only show between levels, after a 5-second warning card, and not until the end of the third finished level. If you see an ad that seems wrong for children, email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with what it showed; AdMob lets us block that advertiser.

### How can my child play Puzzle Jar without ads?

There are two ways. Buy Remove Ads once ($5.99 in the US, shown in your currency), which turns off all full-screen ads for good on that store account; rewarded videos remain, but only play if someone taps "watch ad". Or let your child play with the phone in airplane mode: the games all work, and new ads can't download. Our money and ads page explains both in detail.

### What data does Puzzle Jar collect?

We, the studio, collect no personal information: no account, no name, email, contacts, photos or microphone. Your progress stays on the phone. Google's AdMob, which shows the ads, collects device data: the advertising ID, device type and settings, an approximate location from the IP address, how ads are used, and crash and diagnostic details. On Android only, Google Analytics for Firebase also records game events. The full lists are in our iPhone privacy policy and Android privacy policy .

### Does Puzzle Jar ask for my child's name or email?

No. There is no sign-up, no login and no form anywhere in the app. Puzzle Jar never asks for a name, birthday, email address, phone number or photo, and it does not ask for permission to use the camera, microphone, contacts or GPS location. You open it and play.

### What is the "Allow tracking?" question on iPhone?

It is Apple's own question, asked once at the first launch before any ad loads. If you tap "Allow", Google may use the phone's advertising identifier to show ads based on your interests. If you tap "Ask App Not to Track", ads still show, but they are less personalized. The game works exactly the same either way. You can change the answer later in iPhone Settings, under Privacy & Security, then Tracking.

### Does Puzzle Jar use analytics?

On Android, yes; on iPhone, no. The Android version sends a few events to Google Analytics for Firebase: a won level, milestones at 5, 10, 20 and 50 wins, the value of a purchase, and ad income recorded by Google's ad code. We use them to see whether our Google Ads bring real players. The iPhone version has this switched off.

### What are the "Privacy choices" in Settings?

In Europe, the UK and Switzerland, Google shows a consent form at the first launch asking how your data may be used for ads. The "Privacy choices" button in Puzzle Jar's Settings opens that form again, so you can change your answers at any time. Outside those regions the button does not appear, because the form is not used there.

### Does Puzzle Jar know where I live?

Not from us. The app does not ask for GPS or location permission and has no use for it. Google's ad network does work out a rough area, such as a country or city, from the internet address of the connection, to pick ads in the right language and region. On Android, Google Analytics for Firebase also works out a rough area the same way, and we only see it as totals, such as how many players came from each country.

### How do I delete my child's Puzzle Jar data?

Delete the app. Everything the game itself keeps, from progress and streaks to helpers and settings, lives only on the phone, so removing the app removes it. We hold no account or server copy of progress; the only data we see are, on Android, Google Analytics totals that are not tied to a name. Data Google collects for ads is covered by Google's own policies. On Android you can reset or delete the advertising ID in the phone's settings; on iPhone, answering "Ask App Not to Track" stops the app from using it.

### Can young children play Puzzle Jar without reading?

Mostly, yes. The games are about colors and shapes, with no words, numbers or spelling to solve. The rules cards use short English sentences, so a child who can't read yet may need a grown-up to show the first level; level 1 of each game also has a glowing guide and can't be lost. The menus and buttons are in English only.

### Is Puzzle Jar good for color-blind players?

We designed for it. In the sorting and matching games, each color also carries its own mark or shape, such as a heart, star or tick on a screw, so pieces can be matched by mark alone. Other games give each kind of fruit, sea creature or good its own outline. If a color pair still gives you trouble in one game, tell us which.

### Is Puzzle Jar good for seniors?

Many of our games suit an unhurried player well. There are no lives and nothing to wait for, 19 of the 20 games have no clock, and every level can be retried for free. Hints show a safe move when you're stuck. Pieces are bright and, in most games, marked by shape as well as color. One honest limit: there's no setting for bigger text, and the app is English only.

### Are there timers in Puzzle Jar that rush you?

Only in one mode. Solo Run, inside Route Duel, races a clock: you clear a board alone before the time runs out. Everywhere else there is no countdown. Some games limit moves or pieces instead, which you can plan with at your own pace, and Quilt Pins quietly measures how long a quilt takes only to choose the next one's difficulty, without ever showing a clock.

### Does Puzzle Jar have flashing effects?

There are bright effects on a win, such as confetti, fireworks and glowing pieces. Turning on "Reduce motion" in Settings stops the confetti and some glows. It does not remove every animation, because pieces still have to move to be played. If someone in your family is sensitive to flashing light, try a few levels yourself first.

### Will Puzzle Jar keep my child playing for hours?

We tried not to build it that way. There are no lives that refill on a timer, no "come back in 2 hours" chests and no push notifications calling you back. There is a day streak, which counts days in a row with a finished level, and a broken streak can be saved with a video, so be aware of that pull. Your phone's own Screen Time or Digital Wellbeing limits work with Puzzle Jar like any app.

### Is Puzzle Jar educational?

It's a game first, but it does exercise planning. Most levels reward thinking a few moves ahead, sorting by more than one property, and noticing what blocks what. Quilt Pins is pure logic: every quilt is solved by reasoning, without guessing. We don't make claims beyond that; Puzzle Jar was not designed with teachers or tested in classrooms.

### Are puzzle games good for your brain?

Honestly, the research is mixed. Studies of "brain training" often find that people get better at the games they practice, while proof that this improves memory or thinking in daily life is weaker. We don't claim Puzzle Jar makes anyone smarter or prevents memory loss. What it does offer is a quiet challenge that asks you to plan, look and try again.

### Do puzzle games help with anxiety?

Some people find that a calm puzzle with no clock helps them settle their mind for a few minutes, and that is the kind of game we set out to make. But a game is not a treatment, and we make no health claims. If anxiety is affecting your daily life, please talk to a doctor or a mental health professional.

### Can two children share Puzzle Jar on one phone?

They can, but they'll share one set of progress. Puzzle Jar has no profiles, so the level road, the jar, the streak and the helper counts are the same for everyone who plays on that phone. Free play helps a little: each game keeps its own level, so one child can stick to Bubble Picnic and another to Nut Sort.

### Where can I read Puzzle Jar's privacy policy?

There are two, one for each phone, because the ad and payment set-ups differ: the iPhone privacy policy and the Android privacy policy . Both list what Google collects for ads, what stays on the phone and how to change your tracking and consent choices. Questions go to sultanofniyyat@gmail.com.

## Help: phones, progress, settings and support

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/puzzle-jar/help/

Puzzle Jar runs on iPhone with iOS 15 or newer and on phones with Android 7.0 or newer. Your progress is saved only on the phone: there is no account and no cloud save, so deleting the app deletes your progress, while Restore purchases brings back Remove Ads. For anything not answered here, email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with your phone model and the version number from Settings.

### Which iPhones can run Puzzle Jar?

Any iPhone with iOS 15 or newer. The game runs full screen, in portrait, and the board fits itself to the screen size. An iPhone that is stuck on iOS 14 or earlier can't install it. To check your version, open Settings, then General, then About, and look at iOS Version.

### Is there an iPad version of Puzzle Jar?

No. Puzzle Jar is built for iPhone only, and we don't make an iPad version at the moment. iPads can sometimes run iPhone apps in a phone-sized window, but we don't test Puzzle Jar that way, so we can't promise how it looks or plays. If an iPad version would matter to you, tell us at sultanofniyyat@gmail.com; it helps us decide what to build next.

### Does Puzzle Jar work on iPhone Duo?

Yes. Puzzle Jar supports both screens of iPhone Duo, the outer one you use when the phone is closed and the bigger inner one when it is open, and fills whichever one you are using. The game plays in portrait on both, with the same levels and the same saved progress, since it is one app on one phone.

### Which Android phones can run Puzzle Jar?

Phones with Android 7.0 or newer, which covers most Android phones in use today. It's built for both 32-bit (ARMv7) and 64-bit (ARM64) processors, so older budget phones are included. If Google Play says your device isn't compatible, it is most often because the phone has an older Android version.

### Does Puzzle Jar work on Android tablets?

Possibly, but we can't promise it. We haven't blocked tablets, but we design and test Puzzle Jar on phones, in portrait, so on a large tablet the layout may look stretched or leave empty space. If Google Play offers it on your tablet, you're welcome to try it. Please tell us how it looks.

### How big is the Puzzle Jar download?

On iPhone, about 106 MB. On Android, Google Play shows the exact size for your phone on the install page, because Android downloads are built for each phone. After that, no extra level packs are downloaded: all 20 games and their levels are in that first download, and later changes arrive as normal app updates.

### What languages is Puzzle Jar in?

The app itself is in English only. The games need very little reading, since they are about colors and shapes, but the rules cards, buttons and messages are in English. The App Store page is written in several languages, so the store description you see may be in your own, even though the game inside is English.

### Do I need an account to play Puzzle Jar?

No. There is no sign-up, login, email or password, and no Facebook or Google sign-in. You download it and play. Purchases are handled by your Apple ID or Google account, the same as any app, but Puzzle Jar never asks you to create anything of its own.

### Where is my Puzzle Jar progress saved?

On your phone, inside the app's own storage. Each finished level, your road level, every game's own level, the jar, the day streak, your hints, take backs and rescues, and your settings are written to the phone straight away. We keep no copy on a server, which is why the game works offline and why we never need an account from you.

### Does Puzzle Jar have cloud save?

No, there is no cloud save, no iCloud or Google sync and no Game Center. That's the downside of not having accounts: we can't move or recover your progress, because we don't store it anywhere. Only purchases are kept by the store, and you get them back with Restore purchases.

### What happens to my progress if I delete Puzzle Jar?

It is deleted with the app. Your levels, streak, jar and any unused hints, take backs and rescues are lost, and reinstalling starts you again at level 1 with the welcome gift. One-time purchases are safe: after reinstalling, tap Restore purchases in Settings. If you only want to free up space, check first whether there is another way, such as offloading other apps.

### How do I move my Puzzle Jar progress to a new phone?

The game can't move it for you, because it has no account or cloud save. On the new phone you start again from level 1, then tap Restore purchases in Settings to get back Remove Ads and other one-time purchases. A full phone-to-phone transfer or backup restore made by Apple or Google may bring app data across, but we haven't tested that, so please don't count on it.

### Can I play on an iPhone and an Android phone with the same progress?

No. Each phone keeps its own progress, and nothing is shared between them. Purchases don't cross over either: something bought on the App Store belongs to your Apple ID, and something bought on Google Play belongs to your Google account. Two iPhones on the same Apple ID can each restore Remove Ads, but each still has its own levels.

### What happens if I leave a level halfway?

You start that level again next time. Tapping back during a level asks "Leave this level?", and leaving throws away the moves made on that try. Helpers already spent on it are not refunded, but you lose no level, no streak day and no money, and no ad plays. Your road and game levels stay where they were.

### Why does Puzzle Jar crash or not open?

Try these in order: close the app fully and open it again; restart the phone; update Puzzle Jar from the store; make sure the phone has some free storage; update the phone's system if an update is waiting. Please don't delete and reinstall as a first step, because that erases your progress. If it still crashes, email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with your phone model, its iOS or Android version, the Puzzle Jar version and what you were doing.

### Why isn't my Puzzle Jar purchase going through?

Usually it's the store connection or the store account, not the game. Check that you have internet, that you're signed in to the App Store or Google Play, and that your payment method there works. Purchase restrictions such as Ask to Buy or Screen Time can also stop it. If money was taken but nothing arrived, tap Restore purchases in Settings; for a hint pack, write to us at sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with the store receipt.

### What does "Couldn't reach the App Store" mean?

It means Puzzle Jar couldn't get an answer from the store, so nothing was bought or restored. On Android the message says Google Play instead. The usual causes are no internet, airplane mode, or the store being briefly unavailable. Connect to wifi or mobile data, wait a moment and tap the button again. Your purchases are safe with the store in the meantime.

### How do I turn off sound or music in Puzzle Jar?

Open Settings from the Home screen. Sound and Music are separate switches: Sound controls the taps, pops and win jingles, and Music controls the background tune. Turn off one, the other or both. The choice is remembered for all 20 games, and the phone's own volume buttons work as normal too.

### How do I turn off vibration in Puzzle Jar?

Switch off Vibration in Settings. The game uses short buzzes as feedback, for example when you get stuck on a level; with the switch off, the phone stays still. The one switch covers all 20 games, and the choice is kept until you change it.

### What does Reduce motion do in Puzzle Jar?

It calms the screen down. With Reduce motion on, win confetti is turned off and some glowing halos and extra effects are skipped, while the pieces still move as they must for the game to work. It is useful if busy movement is tiring or distracting. You'll find the switch in Settings, under Vibration.

### How do I see a game's rules again?

Tap the "?" button while playing. Each game shows its rules automatically the first time you open it, and the "?" button brings the same rules card back whenever you want it, without restarting the level. Each game also has its own page on this site with fuller rules and tips, linked from our home page .

### How do I update Puzzle Jar?

Through your phone's store. On iPhone, open the App Store, tap your profile picture and pull down to refresh the list of updates, then tap Update next to Puzzle Jar. On Android, open Google Play, tap your profile picture, then the section for managing your apps and device, and update it there. Updating keeps your progress; only deleting the app removes it.
